S20261102-26.s: Zelensky said Ukrainian forces struck the Kamensky chemical plant in Rostov Oblast, a missile-related facility, and air defence assets, causing about $70 million in damage.

S20261102-27.h: Drones set Kstovo refinery ablaze in Nizhny Novgorod; petrol rationed
S20261102-27.s: Ukrainian drones struck an industrial facility in Kstovo, reportedly the Lukoil refinery, causing a major fire. Moscow reported significant damage at the site. Regional authorities limited petrol sales to 40 litres per car after queues formed.

S20261102-28.h: Ukraine downs most of 433 Russian drones in overnight barrage
S20261102-28.s: Ukraine's air defence downed or jammed 371 of 433 Russian drones launched overnight, with hits at 16 locations. On 1 November it neutralised 274 of 326 drones and all six Banderol missiles.

S20261102-29.h: Russian strikes on energy grid leave hundreds of thousands without power
S20261102-29.s: Russian attacks on substations and energy facilities in at least four regions killed one person, injured 47 and cut power to hundreds of thousands ahead of winter. Over 650 settlements in Zhytomyr Oblast lost electricity, and Kyiv introduced emergency outages. Zelensky called for faster Patriot deliveries.

S20261102-30.h: Russian strikes in Vinnytsia Oblast kill civilians, damage energy sites
S20261102-30.s: Russian attacks on Koziatyn and other parts of Vinnytsia Oblast killed civilians, including a girl and two people at a vocational school dormitory, and injured others. Energy facilities, a mobile phone mast and apartment blocks were damaged.

S20261102-31.h: Oleshky ceasefire allows civilian evacuation, then expires without violations
S20261102-31.s: A US-mediated localised truce, welcomed by Melania Trump, let Ukraine evacuate civilians from occupied Oleshky, with 17 buses and 167 people from the Dnipro's right bank. The six-day ceasefire ended with no violations reported. Bodies of 47 civilians were moved to Henichesk, and Ukraine's foreign minister proposed it as a step toward wider peace.

S20261102-32.h: Kremlin proposes trilateral talks, says Putin would take Zelensky call
S20261102-32.s: Kremlin aide Ushakov proposed initial trilateral US-Russia-Ukraine talks, with Europeans possibly joining later. He said Putin would take a call from Zelensky and that Zelensky is welcome in Moscow. Peskov said Europe must change its stance of defeating Russia to take part.
S20261102-32.t: Türkiye is positioned as a possible venue for any leader-level meeting.

S20261102-33.h: Trump says he may invite Zelensky to December G20 in Florida
S20261102-33.s: Trump said he has no problem inviting Zelensky to the G20 summit in the US in December, after Washington invited Putin. Zelensky said Ukraine has not received an official invitation, and Trump said a Ukraine-Russia peace deal is getting closer.

S20261102-34.h: Rubio reportedly tells allies Ukraine NATO membership unrealistic short-term
S20261102-34.s: Marco Rubio reportedly told Western counterparts that short-term NATO membership for Ukraine is unrealistic and doubts a near-term peace deal.

S20261102-35.h: Russia says it hit vessel and railway station near Odesa
S20261102-35.s: Russia's defence ministry said it struck a vessel carrying military cargo for the Ukrainian army near Odesa and a railway station, and that drone attacks on such ships continue.
S20261102-35.t: Strikes on Black Sea shipping directly affect Türkiye's maritime security and the grain corridor.

S20261102-36.h: Drones enter Romanian and Moldovan airspace during Russian attack
S20261102-36.s: Romania scrambled four F-16s and a helicopter after two drones entered its airspace on 31 October, with no crashes reported. Two drones also violated Moldovan airspace during the massive Russian attack on Ukraine.

S20261102-37.h: Israeli opposition moves to build government as Herzog begins consultations
S20261102-37.s: After the 27 October election left neither bloc with 61 seats, Bennett's party backed Eisenkot to form the next government. Herzog must nominate a candidate by November 11 and urged flexibility, while the Joint List and Ra'am prepare to recommend Eisenkot. The opposition is weighing options such as a one-time direct election, while UTJ may withhold its recommendation.

S20261102-38.h: Israeli election officials reject Netanyahu's foreign-interference claims
S20261102-38.s: Israel's election chief said suspicions of foreign interference, including an inquiry into alleged foreign funding of the Raam party, do not undermine the result. Netanyahu claims the election was stolen. Shin Bet chief David Zini wants to broaden the interference probe, and Haaretz argues Shin Bet and police helped inflate the Qatari-influence allegations.

S20261102-39.h: Israeli siege of Hebron displaces thousands in tenth day
S20261102-39.s: Israel's siege of Hebron has displaced almost 5,000 people, kept nearly 80,000 students out of school and involved home demolitions and arrests. Israeli forces are threatening a wider offensive.

S20261102-40.h: Israeli strikes kill at least eight in Gaza despite ceasefire
S20261102-40.s: Israeli drone and air strikes in Gaza City, Khan Younis and elsewhere killed at least eight to nine Palestinians, including five police officers and a child.

S20261102-41.h: Syria foils sabotage plot against Homs oil refinery
S20261102-41.s: Syrian security forces foiled a sabotage plot against the Homs oil refinery, seizing suicide vests, explosive devices and facility maps.

S20261102-42.s: Incumbent Iliana Iotova, who opposes military aid to Ukraine, won the Bulgarian presidential runoff by a wide margin over Andrei Gyurov, amid record low turnout.

S20261102-43.h: European diplomats fear US troop cuts if Trump loses midterms
S20261102-43.s: European diplomats fear Trump could withdraw thousands more troops from Europe or cut NATO funding if he loses the midterms.

S20261102-44.h: DEM's Sancar says Öcalan moved to new İmralı home, urges faster PKK process
S20261102-44.s: DEM Party's Mithat Sancar says Abdullah Öcalan has moved to a new İmralı home and urged Türkiye to speed up the stalled PKK peace process.
S20261102-44.t: The stalled process affects both Türkiye's internal security and its Syria policy.

S20261102-45.h: Mazloum Abdi says SDF integration into Syrian state continues despite attempts to derail it
S20261102-45.s: Mazloum Abdi said in Qamishli that efforts to integrate the SDF into the Syrian state continue despite attempts to derail them.
S20261102-45.t: SDF integration is central to Ankara's demands on northeast Syria and the PKK file.

S20261103-01.h: Iran says revised seven-step plan could reopen Hormuz within two days if US lifts blockade
S20261103-01.s: Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Baghaei said a condensed seven-stage plan could take effect within two days if Washington ends its naval blockade and meets Iran's demands. Tehran says the ball is in the US court. It also rejects transferring enriched uranium abroad, and Araghchi says full talks can resume only once its Hormuz terms are met.
S20261103-01.t: A Hormuz reopening or a renewed war would directly affect Türkiye's energy import costs and regional security.

S20261103-02.h: Qatari mediators carry US-Iran draft deal as Iranian delegation leaves Doha
S20261103-02.s: Iran says intensive indirect talks via Qatar and Pakistan continue, though the Doha round ended without a breakthrough. A draft agreement negotiated over about eight days is circulating for feedback. A Qatari delegation is expected in Tehran, and a follow-up meeting is possible.
S20261103-02.t: Türkiye has an interest in the mediation succeeding because it reduces the risk of a regional war on its border.

S20261103-03.h: Vance reports progress with Iran and is optimistic about a negotiated settlement
S20261103-03.s: Vice President Vance said the US and Iran have made progress toward a settlement and that he and Trump feel good about it. Trump said he believes Tehran wants a deal. Iran insists the US must first lift its blockade and meet its demands in full.

S20261103-04.h: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei empowers government to negotiate with US
S20261103-04.s: President Pezeshkian said the Supreme Leader granted the government powers to resolve the dispute with the US through dialogue. This is a signal of top-level backing for the diplomatic track.

S20261103-05.h: US struck Iran's Qeshm island in secret series of limited strikes, officials say
S20261103-05.s: The WSJ reported, and US officials confirmed, that US forces struck Qeshm island as part of limited strikes carried out secretly in recent weeks. A US official called them defensive responses to Iranian surface-to-air fire. Iranian media reported five blasts on the island and near Bandar Lengeh.
S20261103-05.t: The covert strikes show that the ceasefire is fragile, which raises escalation risk for Türkiye's neighbourhood.

S20261103-06.h: IRGC claims it downed or captured several US drones over Hormuz
S20261103-06.s: The IRGC said it shot down two MQM-170 drones south of Qeshm, an MQ-9, and captured a fourth US reconnaissance drone intact. Some of the claims cite electronic warfare. They are Iranian claims and are not independently confirmed in these items.

S20261103-07.h: Netanyahu reportedly urged Trump to resume Iran strikes after midterms
S20261103-07.s: Axios reported that Netanyahu pressed Trump on 31 October to resume strikes after the US midterms. Israel's UN envoy denied it. Tucker Carlson alleged Netanyahu wants a strike on a suspected nuclear site, and Trump confirmed a 'very good' call about Iran.
S20261103-07.t: Israeli pressure for a renewed Iran war would put Türkiye under strain as a neighbour.

S20261103-08.h: Trump says no plan to strike Iran before or right after midterms, but threat remains
S20261103-08.s: Trump said he is not considering renewed strikes right after the midterms and is in no hurry, though he said the US will eventually have to strike hard if there is no deal. Axios and others reported he prefers to let talks play out, while Tehran warns a new war would last longer.

S20261103-09.h: Iran says tankers hit mines on unauthorised Hormuz routes; IRGC cites 11 fires
S20261103-09.s: The IRGC Navy said 11 tankers caught fire between 25 October and 2 November, some sinking, after violating passage rules. Iranian military statements say further tankers hit mines east of the strait on unauthorised routes with navigation systems off.

S20261103-10.h: Vessels struck by projectiles near Hormuz and Gulf; CENTCOM accuses Iran
S20261103-10.s: UKMTO reported ships hit by unknown projectiles near Hormuz, off Oman and off Saudi Arabia, with crews safe. CENTCOM accused Iran of deliberately attacking civilian mariners and Gulf sites, while reports suggest the real number of attacks exceeds the official count. The Arab League and GCC condemned an attack on a Qatari LNG tanker.

S20261103-11.h: Oil prices drop 6-8% as US-Iran diplomacy eases Hormuz fears
S20261103-11.s: Brent fell as much as 8% to below $105 and later below $104, its lowest since 15 October, on hopes for a deal. European gas prices also dropped.
S20261103-11.t: Lower oil and gas prices would ease Türkiye's energy import bill.

S20261103-12.h: Gulf states fear becoming targets as Trump threatens Iran; some warned Tehran
S20261103-12.s: Trump's threats have renewed Gulf fears that US bases make them targets for Iranian reprisal. The WSJ reports some Arab states warned Iran they could retaliate individually or collectively if their infrastructure is hit.

S20261103-13.h: Türkiye's parliament to debate Mecca Agreement; Syria considers joining
S20261103-13.s: The joint defence agreement among Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia goes to the TBMM General Assembly on Wednesday. Syria says it is in talks about joining what is called the Mecca Alliance, and Russia welcomed Iran's meeting with Mecca Pact countries.
S20261103-13.t: Ratification would formalise a trilateral defence pact and could widen Türkiye's security umbrella to include Syria.

S20261103-14.h: Öcalan moved to prison villa on İmralı, expected to boost peace process role
S20261103-14.s: Türkiye moved Abdullah Öcalan to a new section or residence on İmralı island, improving his conditions, a key Kurdish demand. DEM lawmakers called for further steps in the peace process.
S20261103-14.t: The move signals Ankara's commitment to the process to end PKK violence and could give Öcalan a more direct negotiating role.

S20261103-15.h: DEM Party ends urban accord with CHP; Demirtaş detention seen hampering process
S20261103-15.s: The DEM Party ended its alliance with the CHP from the 2024 local elections, and council members will serve within DEM. Roj Girasun said Demirtaş's detention has hampered the peace process.
S20261103-15.t: The change in the opposition landscape and the Demirtaş case could affect how the process unfolds domestically.

S20261103-16.h: Russian bombs kill 24 at aid centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia
S20261103-16.s: Russian aerial bombs hit a school used as a humanitarian aid centre in Komyshuvakha and then a shelter, killing 24 according to Ukrainian officials; 27 people are reported missing. Zelensky said Russia rejects de-escalation, and the region declared a day of mourning.

S20261103-17.h: US announces Russia-Ukraine-US talks in Abu Dhabi on 10-11 November
S20261103-17.s: Witkoff said trilateral working-level talks will be held in Abu Dhabi on security guarantees and ending the war, with Witkoff and Kushner expected to attend. Witkoff will first consult European allies in Brussels.
S20261103-17.t: The venue is in the Gulf rather than Türkiye, which sidelines Ankara's mediation ambitions.

S20261103-18.h: Zelensky ready to meet Putin in Turkey, names Türkiye a realistic mediator
S20261103-18.s: Zelensky said he is ready for a trilateral summit in Türkiye if Erdoğan's mediation succeeds, and called Türkiye a practical mediator. He also proposed Black Sea security rules.
S20261103-18.t: It reinforces Ankara's claim to a mediating role and a say in Black Sea security arrangements.

S20261103-19.h: US floats restoring Russian gas to Europe via Ukraine; EU resists
S20261103-19.s: The WSJ reports a US proposal, tied to energy ceasefire talks, to send Russian gas to Europe through Ukrainian pipelines with revenue in escrow or via an American intermediary. EU officials and Lithuania reject it, and Peskov said transit is hardly possible now.
S20261103-19.t: Any change in Russian gas routes affects Türkiye's ambition to be a regional gas hub.

S20261103-20.h: Oleshky ceasefire expires; Russia refuses extension and reinforces positions
S20261103-20.s: The six-day US-coordinated truce in occupied Oleshky, which allowed aid and evacuation of about 800 civilians, ended on 1-2 November. Russia refused to extend it and Ukraine says Moscow used it to rotate and resupply troops. Fighting resumed, and the Kremlin rules out further pauses.

S20261103-21.h: Russia presses mass drone and missile campaign on Ukraine's energy sector
S20261103-21.s: Russia launched 171 drones and 10 missiles on 2 November, and attacked energy infrastructure 94 times in a week. Zelensky warned of a new large-scale strike on energy and logistics. Ukraine's intelligence also detailed the upgraded Gerbera-2 attack drone and Russian Shaheds with bigger antennas.

S20261103-22.h: Ukraine strikes Russian refineries and oil storage; Zelensky links halt to Patriots
S20261103-22.s: Ukrainian drones reportedly hit the Yaroslavl refinery and a large oil storage site in Samara, and a Su-57 was lost at Akhtubinsk, possibly linked to degraded fuel. Zelensky said strikes will stop if the US supplies Patriots or Russia stops attacking energy sites.

S20261103-23.h: US approves $2.1bn Patriot sale to Ukraine, deliveries only from 2030
S20261103-23.s: The State Department approved 500 PAC-3 interceptors for Ukraine, delivered between late 2030 and 2033. The Netherlands and partners are exploring ways to speed up Patriot delivery, and Germany and the UK are working on air defence for Ukraine.

S20261103-24.h: NATO allies fear US troop and funding cuts if Republicans lose midterms
S20261103-24.s: Politico reports allies fear Trump could cut troops, alliance funding and Ukraine arms sales after a Republican midterm loss. The US is also reportedly preparing to seek extra NATO funding for the Ukraine weapons programme, and European troops will rehearse a post-peace Ukraine deployment.
S20261103-24.t: Any US drawdown from NATO raises Türkiye's weight in the alliance's southern and eastern flanks.

S20261103-25.h: Poland reinforces Russian border after sabotage warnings; Latvia hit by stray drones
S20261103-25.s: Poland deployed counterterrorism police and is converting a unit into a border brigade after intelligence warnings of Russian sabotage and incursions from Kaliningrad. Latvia raised alerts after drones entered its airspace, and a NATO aircraft patrolled near Kaliningrad.

S20261103-26.h: Russia-friendly Iliana Yotova wins Bulgaria's presidential runoff
S20261103-26.s: Yotova won with 57.58% against pro-Western Andrey Gurov. She backs dialogue with Moscow and opposes military aid to Ukraine.
S20261103-26.t: A Russia-friendly president in Bulgaria, Türkiye's Black Sea neighbour, changes the EU and NATO balance on Ukraine.

S20261103-27.h: Belgian PM De Wever resigns after budget talks fail
S20261103-27.s: De Wever submitted his resignation to King Philippe after 2027 budget talks collapsed. The king will consult coalition leaders.

S20261103-28.h: Cyberattacks hit Russian and Ukrainian alert apps and European supermarket fridges
S20261103-28.s: Both Russia and Ukraine say their emergency alert apps were hacked, sending fake nuclear alerts, and Zelensky confirmed a retaliatory hack. Separately, suspected hackers remotely raised temperatures in supermarket fridges in seven European countries.

S20261103-29.h: Israel's election leaves Netanyahu short of majority; Eisenkot gains opposition backing
S20261103-29.s: Final results give Netanyahu's bloc 53 seats, Eisenkot's 48 and Arab-led parties a record 19. Lieberman, Bennett, Golan, Democrats and Arab parties back Eisenkot while Netanyahu calls for a broad government without Arab parties. Herzog begins consultations.
S20261103-29.t: A Netanyahu exit or a prolonged deadlock would shape Israel's posture toward Syria and Türkiye.

S20261103-30.h: Likud and Shin Bet chief raise foreign-interference claims over Israeli election
S20261103-30.s: Haaretz reports Shin Bet chief Zini wanted results delayed over alleged foreign influence, then reversed. Likud sought an urgent briefing, which the elections committee chief rejected, and Eisenkot accused Netanyahu of trying to discredit the results.

S20261103-31.h: Israel ends Hebron operation as West Bank settler attacks hit record
S20261103-31.s: The IDF withdrew from Hebron after a 10-day operation that displaced about 3,300 people, and residents are returning. UN data show 397 settler attacks in October, the highest monthly total since 2006.

S20261103-32.h: Israeli strikes continue in Gaza and Lebanon despite ceasefires
S20261103-32.s: Israeli strikes killed several Palestinians in Gaza, with over 1,580 killed since the October ceasefire, and Israel also shelled southern Lebanon. Lebanese fears of another war have grown after Israeli reports.

S20261103-33.h: Houthis escalate attacks on Saudi Arabia; coalition intercepts missiles and drones
S20261103-33.s: The Houthis claimed drone attacks on Dammam airport and Jizan sites, and the coalition intercepted a ballistic missile and two drones over Riyadh. Saudi civil defence issued alerts across southern and western cities and later lifted some. The US warned citizens and the EU condemned the escalation.
S20261103-33.t: Türkiye is Saudi Arabia's partner in the new defence pact, so the Houthi war could draw it in.

S20261103-34.h: Saudi strikes hit Hodeidah as Houthis advance toward Aden
S20261103-34.s: Saudi strikes hit Hodeidah ports and an oil facility, wounding seven. Houthis are reportedly within 80 km of Aden, fighting resumed on the Bab al-Mandab front, and a Houthi missile hit a Lahij health centre, injuring about 20. Saudi and US defence chiefs discussed de-escalation.

S20261103-35.h: China sends envoys and urges dialogue on Iran war as Xi hosts Oman's sultan
S20261103-35.s: Wang Yi told Iran's Ali Bagheri Kani in Beijing that China backs Iran's sovereignty and opposes renewed confrontation. China will send special envoys to Iran, Oman, Saudi Arabia and Egypt, and Xi told Oman's sultan the Gulf must not become an arena of great-power rivalry.

S20261103-36.h: Russia and Iran coordinate diplomacy; Moscow keeps uranium transfer offer open
S20261103-36.s: Rezaei and Putin reaffirmed strategic cooperation, and Russia's foreign ministry discussed the Gulf and Yemen with Iran. Moscow said uranium removal was not raised in US consultations while Putin's transfer proposal remains on the table.

S20261103-37.h: Erdoğan in South Korea offers Sinop nuclear partnership and defence cooperation
S20261103-37.s: Erdoğan arrived in Seoul and proposed South Korean partnership in the Sinop nuclear plant, AI, defence and semiconductors. A $15bn bilateral trade target was set, with financing the key factor.
S20261103-37.t: The visit could secure financing and technology for Türkiye's nuclear programme and defence industry.

S20261103-38.h: Türkiye begins serial production plan for SİPER-2 air defence in 2027
S20261103-38.s: Minister Kacır said serial production of the SİPER-2 long-range air defence system will begin in 2027, as part of the Çelik Kubbe architecture.
S20261103-38.t: It advances Türkiye's indigenous layered air defence amid regional missile threats.

S20261103-39.h: Türkiye nominated for UN Secretary-General; Sinirlioğlu enters race
S20261103-39.s: Latvia assumed the UN Security Council presidency and officially nominated Türkiye for the next Secretary-General. Erdoğan confidant Feridun Sinirlioğlu has entered the race.
S20261103-39.t: A Turkish SG candidacy would raise Ankara's diplomatic profile.

S20261103-40.h: Cyprus talks revive as Holguin meets leaders; Türkiye vows energy activity
S20261103-40.s: UN envoy Holguin met Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman and will meet Christodoulides to prepare a trilateral meeting. Turkish Cypriot leader Üstel said Türkiye and the Turkish Cypriot side will continue Eastern Mediterranean energy activity without seeking permission. Cyprus says Great Sea Interconnector surveys are on schedule, and north Cyprus votes on 6 December.
S20261103-40.t: Cyprus talks and the interconnector surveys bear directly on Ankara's Eastern Mediterranean positions.

S20261103-41.h: Greece buys three Embraer KC-390 transports from Portugal
S20261103-41.s: Greece signed a government-to-government deal worth up to €600m for three KC-390s with options for more. Dendias said mid-air refuelling would have prevented the 1974 Turkish invasion of Cyprus.
S20261103-41.t: The Greek airlift and refuelling upgrade is a force-projection step relevant to Aegean and Cyprus balances.

S20261103-42.h: Savcı Sayan fund probe fuels AKP infighting; İBB trial continues
S20261103-42.s: Commentator Ruşen Çakır says the fund investigation has reignited score-settling within the AKP. Meanwhile, the Sarıgül probe has reached Özgür Özel, who denies receiving money, and the third İBB hearing began.

S20261103-43.h: Syria appoints Druze adviser for peace affairs; studies new Turkish border crossing
S20261103-43.s: Damascus appointed Druze figure Muzna al-Atrash from Suwayda as a peace adviser as it seeks authority in the south. Syria's customs authority is studying new crossings including Qamishli-Nusaybin with Türkiye, and Lebanese officials held talks in Damascus on border and refugees.
S20261103-43.t: A new Qamishli-Nusaybin crossing would extend Türkiye's economic reach in north-east Syria.

S20261103-44.h: Iraqi crude flows to Ceyhan via Kurdistan pipeline; Baghdad armed-groups deal unsigned
S20261103-44.s: SOMO reportedly sends 500,000 barrels a day through the Kurdistan pipeline to Ceyhan, unconfirmed by officials. Separately, a Hoquq bloc head said the Coordination Framework and armed groups agreed on weapons but PM al-Zaidi has not signed, and Erbil airport is resuming flights.
S20261103-44.t: The flow of Iraqi oil via Ceyhan would help Türkiye's role as an energy transit hub, amid Hormuz disruption.

S20261103-45.h: Qatar and UAE move to hedge against Hormuz disruption
S20261103-45.s: Qatar is securing long-term US LNG supplies while mediating, and the UAE's SNOC says it could build a 100 km pipeline bypassing Hormuz.

S20261104-01.h: US launches limited 'defensive' strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island near Hormuz
S20261104-01.s: US forces struck an Iranian coastal anti-aircraft site on Qeshm Island overnight, hours after Vance and Trump signalled diplomatic progress. US officials call the strikes limited and defensive, a response to IRGC fire on a US aircraft, not a resumption of major combat. Trump confirmed the strike and Iranian media reported explosions.
S20261104-01.t: Renewed US-Iran fighting around Hormuz threatens Türkiye's energy supply, regional stability and its mediation role alongside Saudi Arabia and Pakistan.

S20261104-02.h: Trump announces end of roughly $4 billion annual US military aid to Israel
S20261104-02.s: Trump said the US will end its annual military aid to Israel after this year, saying he agreed this with Netanyahu and describing Israel as self-sufficient. Weapons sales will continue, and he said the US would help Israel if needed. The announcement came on US midterm election day.
S20261104-02.t: A weakening of the US-Israel aid relationship shifts regional deterrence calculations and affects Ankara's dealings with both Washington and Israel.

S20261104-03.h: Israeli defence and finance officials stunned by Trump aid cutoff
S20261104-03.s: Israeli defence and finance officials were surprised by the announcement, as talks with the Americans were reportedly ongoing. KAN estimates a $3.8bn annual defence budget shortfall. Opposition figures including Eisenkot and Golan blamed Netanyahu, and Haaretz analysis sees stricter scrutiny of arms sales if Democrats win.
S20261104-03.t: Israeli budget and arms-supply strain could change Israel's regional posture, including in Syria.

S20261104-04.h: Qatar says US and Iran reviewing proposals as mediation continues
S20261104-04.s: Qatar's Foreign Ministry said both Washington and Tehran are studying Doha's proposals and remain committed to mediation. Anadolu reported the US approved a Qatar-presented draft under which Iran would make nuclear concessions for partial release of frozen assets. Qatari officials travelled to Tehran for Iran's reply, while Iranian assessments see a return to war as most likely.
S20261104-04.t: A Qatar-brokered interim deal would ease Hormuz and energy risks that Türkiye is exposed to.

S20261104-05.h: Iranian officials say deal with US remains far; 'ball is in America's court'
S20261104-05.s: A senior Iranian official told Reuters Tehran and Washington remain far from a deal, and Iran rejects excessive US demands. Iran delivered a response via mediators and said the ball is in the US court. Parliament speaker Qalibaf said the military is at highest readiness, and China urged restraint.
S20261104-05.t: Stalled talks keep the risk of renewed war on Türkiye's border and Hormuz energy flows unresolved.

S20261104-06.h: Iran sets conditions on Hormuz and vows response 'without geographic limits'
S20261104-06.s: Iran's security chief said Hormuz will reopen only after the US meets seven conditions. Armed forces chief Abdollahi set five principles for regional security, including sanctions relief, frozen assets and recognition of sovereignty over Hormuz. The IRGC and Qalibaf warned any new US-Israeli attack will meet a broad response, and Iran says it has a 'maximum deterrence' plan.
S20261104-06.t: Iranian claims of sovereignty over Hormuz and threats of regional escalation endanger Turkish trade and energy security.

S20261104-07.h: Iran warns any new war could reach Europe, naming US bases
S20261104-07.s: Iranian officials and hardline lawmakers warned a new confrontation could extend to Europe, naming US military facilities as targets. Hamshahri published a map marking British Akrotiri in Cyprus and Greek military sites. Tehran reportedly raised readiness to its highest level.
S20261104-07.t: Targeting of facilities in Cyprus and Greece, and of US bases in Europe, puts the eastern Mediterranean and NATO territory into the Iran war's risk zone.

S20261104-08.h: Trump says no immediate plans to strike Iran after midterms
S20261104-08.s: Trump told the Financial Times and others that the US has no immediate plans to strike Iran, after Vance reported good Qatar-mediated conversations. He called the Qeshm strike minor and said he does not want to kill many people.
S20261104-08.t: A US posture of waiting rather than striking lowers near-term escalation risk on Türkiye's border.

S20261104-09.h: Three oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, IRGC says
S20261104-09.s: The IRGC Navy said three tankers exploded and caught fire after striking sea mines overnight, blaming use of unauthorised routes.
S20261104-09.t: Mining of Hormuz shipping lanes raises energy prices and shipping risk for Türkiye.

S20261104-10.h: Tanker struck by projectiles off Oman; Indian national killed
S20261104-10.s: UKMTO reported two unidentified objects hit a tanker northeast of Oman's Lima area, with two projectiles in the engine room and no environmental damage reported. India condemned an attack on a ship off Oman that killed an Indian national.

S20261104-11.h: Iran charges Hormuz transit fees to some ships, exempts Qatar, India, China, Iraq
S20261104-11.s: Iranian lawmakers gave conflicting accounts of Hormuz transit rules: one said Indian and Chinese vessels are charged while Qatari ships are exempt, another said ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar are exempt from restrictions.
S20261104-11.t: A selective Hormuz toll regime sets a precedent that could affect Turkish shipping and energy imports.

S20261104-12.h: Iran says talks with Saudi Arabia continue after Saudi-Turkish-Pakistani meeting
S20261104-12.s: Araghchi said talks with Saudi Arabia continue and called for regional security free of foreign military presence. He said Iran bears no hostility toward GCC states. Haaretz linked this to a meeting with Saudi, Turkish and Pakistani officials.
S20261104-12.t: Türkiye is part of an emerging Saudi-Turkish-Pakistani format on Iran, enhancing its diplomatic role.

S20261104-13.h: Israel reportedly tells US Iran weighs chemical weapons; officials split
S20261104-13.s: Israeli intelligence reportedly told US officials that Iran is considering chemical weapons and advancing missile-mounting technology. US officials are divided, some seeing it as an effort to push Trump to resume large-scale strikes, and Gulf states doubt it.
S20261104-13.t: A new WMD narrative could be used to justify renewed war next to Türkiye.

S20261104-14.h: Netanyahu reportedly presses Trump to hit Iran after midterms
S20261104-14.s: Officials say Netanyahu is pushing Trump to attack Iran after the US midterms. Haaretz reports Israeli military reluctance to join a possible US strike, with the leaders pursuing different goals.
S20261104-14.t: A joint US-Israeli strike on Iran would hit Türkiye's neighbourhood with refugee, trade and security effects.

S20261104-15.h: Oil rises above $105 after Qeshm strikes dim peace hopes
S20261104-15.s: Oil prices rose past $105 after the US strike on Qeshm Island, as peace prospects dimmed.
S20261104-15.t: Higher oil prices worsen Türkiye's import bill and inflation.

S20261104-16.h: Saudi Aramco starts expanding East-West Pipeline to bypass Hormuz
S20261104-16.s: Aramco is expanding the East-West Pipeline to carry up to 10 million barrels per day. Aramco reported a 9% profit rise and cited attacks on the pipeline.
S20261104-16.t: Hormuz bypass routes reshape Gulf-Europe energy flows, relevant to Turkish energy-hub ambitions.

S20261104-17.h: Yemen says 21 IRGC and Hezbollah experts direct Houthi operations
S20261104-17.s: Yemen's interior minister said 21 foreign experts from the IRGC and Hezbollah oversee Houthi military operations across six provinces. Yemen's UN envoy asked the Security Council to act on Iranian arms transfers after a missile killed five in Lahij.

S20261104-18.h: Saudi-led coalition downs more Houthi drones as US warns of attack risks
S20261104-18.s: The coalition intercepted drones over the Eastern Province, Mecca region and southern Saudi Arabia. The US Embassy warned Americans of Houthi attacks and airport risks, and Saudi Arabia said it will defend its sovereignty.

S20261104-19.h: Houthis advance in Lahij toward Bab al-Mandeb and Aden
S20261104-19.s: Houthis intensified fighting in Lahj, claiming progress toward control of Bab al-Mandeb. Yemen reshuffled its cabinet as Houthi forces advanced toward Aden.
S20261104-19.t: Houthi control of Bab al-Mandeb would imperil Red Sea trade routes.

S20261104-20.h: Syria says it foiled Hezbollah-linked plot against Homs refinery
S20261104-20.s: Syrian security forces arrested a cell from Lebanon and seized explosives, saying it planned to attack the Homs refinery. Hezbollah denied the accusation.
S20261104-20.t: Instability and Hezbollah activity in Syria threaten Ankara's stake in Syrian stabilisation and reconstruction.

S20261104-21.h: Damascus tightens crackdown on Hezbollah smuggling routes
S20261104-21.s: Syrian authorities are countering Hezbollah's former smuggling corridors since Assad's fall. A Hezbollah-appointed Lebanese official was nonetheless received by Foreign Minister Shaibani in the first such visit since Assad fell.
S20261104-21.t: A Hezbollah-free Syria supports Turkish aims in Syria.

S20261104-22.h: Syria evaluating joining the Mecca Pact alliance
S20261104-22.s: Foreign Minister Shaibani said Damascus is evaluating joining the Mecca Pact alliance.
S20261104-22.t: Syria's alliance choices affect Türkiye's regional partnerships.

S20261104-23.h: Erdoğan and Lee agree nuclear, defence and trade cooperation in Seoul
S20261104-23.s: Türkiye and South Korea signed agreements on nuclear financing, energy, mining and science. They agreed joint defence production and third-country exports, and a $15 billion trade target, with Seoul seeking a role in Sinop.
S20261104-23.t: The deal advances Sinop nuclear plans and joint defence production with South Korea.

S20261104-24.h: MIT chief Kalın meets UAE's Mansour bin Zayed in Abu Dhabi
S20261104-24.s: Türkiye's intelligence chief visited the UAE and held regional security talks with UAE Vice President Mansour bin Zayed.
S20261104-24.t: Direct intelligence-level contact with Abu Dhabi deepens Türkiye-UAE security coordination amid the Iran crisis.

S20261104-25.h: ASELSAN signs $1.1 billion air defence export contract
S20261104-25.s: ASELSAN signed a $1.1 billion air defence export contract with an unnamed international customer. Turkish defence and aviation exports also rose 61% in October to $1.14bn.
S20261104-25.t: Large export wins strengthen Türkiye's defence industry and its strategic footprint.

S20261104-26.h: Türkiye preparing MUGEM aircraft carrier programme
S20261104-26.s: Türkiye is preparing to enter the aircraft carrier class with MUGEM to protect Blue Homeland interests.
S20261104-26.t: A carrier would project Turkish naval power in the Mediterranean, Aegean and Black Sea.

S20261104-27.h: Turkish investment fund probe widens; ex-Borsa chief arrested
S20261104-27.s: Former Borsa İstanbul chief Ergun was arrested on bribery charges and detention warrants were issued for six more, including former SPK and BDDK officials. The justice minister cites an organised network; 112 of 433 suspects are jailed. CHP's Özel attacked Erdoğan, and a poll shows AKP support down about 3 points.
S20261104-27.t: The scandal erodes market confidence and AKP support domestically.

S20261104-28.h: Türkiye's annual inflation rises to 29.77% in October
S20261104-28.s: TÜİK data show annual inflation at 29.77% and monthly inflation at 2.58%.
S20261104-28.t: Rising inflation adds pressure on the government amid fuel price and market stress.

S20261104-29.h: Cyprus president objects to UN envoy meeting Turkish ambassador in the north
S20261104-29.s: Christodoulides voiced strong dissatisfaction to UN envoy Holguín over her meeting with Turkey's ambassador in the occupied north, ahead of a planned November 9 trilateral with Erhürman.
S20261104-29.t: The row complicates UN-led Cyprus talks and Ankara's position.

S20261104-30.h: Russia launches year's biggest strike on Ukraine's energy grid
S20261104-30.s: Russian missiles and drones hit energy facilities in ten regions, halting three DTEK thermal plants and causing emergency outages and water cuts in Kyiv. Russia says it hit four power plants and two substations. Zelensky said Ukraine resumed refinery strikes in response.
S20261104-30.t: The attacks on Ukraine's energy affect Black Sea security and talks in which Türkiye is a traditional host.

S20261104-31.h: Russian drones target substations critical to Ukrainian nuclear plants
S20261104-31.s: Three drones targeted a substation vital to Khmelnytskyi NPP, prompting a warning from Ukraine's energy minister. A substation in Rivne Oblast, home to another nuclear plant, was also damaged.

S20261104-32.h: Russian glide bombs hit aid site in Komyshuvakha, killing about 30
S20261104-32.s: A Russian strike on an aid distribution site and school shelter in Zaporizhzhia Oblast killed at least 29-33 people, with dozens missing. Latvia called an emergency UN Security Council meeting.

S20261104-33.h: Russian strikes hit hospitals in Kharkiv and Dnipro
S20261104-33.s: Strikes injured 62 people at a Kharkiv medical facility, with over 220 patients evacuated. A jet-powered glide bomb was used, and a Dnipro hospice was also hit.

S20261104-34.h: Russia, Ukraine and US to hold trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November
S20261104-34.s: The Kremlin confirmed Medinsky will lead Russia's delegation. Zelensky listed security guarantees, recovery, an energy ceasefire and Black Sea access as his agenda. Peskov ruled out European participation.
S20261104-34.t: Medinsky's role echoes the Istanbul format, and Türkiye is sidelined from the venue.

S20261104-35.h: Merz hosts Zelensky in Berlin, says Europe must be at the table
S20261104-35.s: Merz said Russia has not yet engaged seriously and Europe must be part of any talks. Germany pledged more air defence and energy aid, and Merz called Putin's G20 invitation unacceptable.
S20261104-35.t: European sidelining from talks shows limits of the format and creates space for others, including Türkiye.

S20261104-36.h: Brussels hosts US-Europe-NATO-Ukraine meeting on reconstruction and guarantees
S20261104-36.s: The European Commission hosted US, UK, French, German, NATO, Ukrainian and World Bank officials on a recovery package and security guarantees ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks.

S20261104-37.h: Kremlin working on Putin-Trump-Xi meeting at APEC in Shenzhen
S20261104-37.s: The Kremlin said it is working to arrange a trilateral meeting on the APEC sidelines in about two weeks, with Beijing leading preparations.
S20261104-37.t: A great-power summit without NATO Europe would affect Türkiye's balancing between Moscow, Washington and Beijing.

S20261104-38.h: Poland deploys special forces to Russian border after sabotage warnings
S20261104-38.s: Tusk said authorities prevented a suspected provocation near the Kaliningrad border after spotting people with flashlights. Counterterrorism units were deployed after intelligence warnings. An unidentified drone also crashed in Latvia.

S20261104-39.h: NATO to boost Black Sea surveillance as shipping strikes widen
S20261104-39.s: NATO will deploy maritime patrol aircraft, radars and drones to the Black Sea after repeated strikes on cargo ships near Romania and Bulgaria. Attacks on shipping threaten grain exports.
S20261104-39.t: A militarised Black Sea directly affects Türkiye's Montreux role and its navy and trade.

S20261104-40.h: Ukrainian drones hit Yaroslavl refinery as Russia reports mass drone downings
S20261104-40.s: Drones started a major fire at the Slavneft-YANOS refinery in Yaroslavl. Russia reported destroying 856 drones, and Ukraine hit at least 30 targets in Russia in October.

S20261104-41.h: Israeli opposition unites behind Eisenkot to oust Netanyahu
S20261104-41.s: Opposition leaders backed Eisenkot for prime minister and vowed a national emergency government but lack a majority without Arab parties. Herzog began consultations, and Likud's bloc won the most seats.
S20261104-41.t: Israeli political deadlock affects Netanyahu's ability to act on Iran, Syria and Türkiye-related files.

S20261104-42.h: Shin Bet bid to question Arab lawmakers over election interference rejected
S20261104-42.s: The Attorney General refused Shin Bet chief Zini's request to probe Arab party leaders, citing lack of evidence. Arab parties and the opposition condemned Zini and Likud attacked the AG.

S20261104-43.h: UK and France to lead 2,800-troop Ukraine force drills in Poland
S20261104-43.s: The Coalition of the Willing will rehearse Multinational Force Ukraine deployment in Poland from November 9–22, which Russia calls a threat. Merz called leaders to Berlin on November 19 to set 2027 military support.

S20261104-44.h: Baghdad integrates PKK-linked YBS fighters into Iraqi forces in Sinjar
S20261104-44.s: Baghdad has begun integrating thousands of YBS fighters into Iraqi forces, sparking a dispute over Yazidi identity.
S20261104-44.t: Formalising PKK-linked fighters in Sinjar cuts against Türkiye's goals in the PKK disarmament process.

S20261105-01.h: Turkish parliament begins ratifying Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
S20261105-01.s: Parliament approved the first article of the bill ratifying the Mecca defence pact among Türkiye, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia. The pact contains a collective defence clause, and ratification comes while Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia continue.
S20261105-01.t: Ratification ties Türkiye into a collective defence commitment with Riyadh and Islamabad during an active Gulf conflict.

S20261105-02.h: IRGC says mines destroyed four tankers in Hormuz and two vessels were seized
S20261105-02.s: The IRGC says four oil tankers that entered a prohibited passage south of the Strait of Hormuz were destroyed by naval mines. It also says two other vessels were seized or halted. Gulf News reports the four tankers caught fire, and Trump said US forces are 'locked and loaded'.
S20261105-02.t: Escalation at Hormuz threatens energy supply and prices on which Türkiye depends.

S20261105-03.h: Vance and Trump blame Iran war for Republican midterm losses
S20261105-03.s: Vice President Vance said the Iran war, cost of living and US-Israel ties drove voters to the Democrats. Trump called it 'largely true' that the war caused the losses, but said he 'had to do it' and would make the same decision again.
S20261105-03.t: Washington's political cost from the Iran war shapes how likely a US exit or escalation is on Türkiye's border.

S20261105-04.h: Democrats take Congress and weigh war-powers limits on Trump's Iran war
S20261105-04.s: Democrats won majorities in both chambers, with Senate control confirmed at 51 seats and Jeffries set to become House speaker. Leaders including Schumer vow to end the Iran war and are weighing war-powers and funding levers, though analysts note they lack veto-override numbers. The incoming Congress will also scrutinise the $1.5 trillion Pentagon budget and the roughly $90 billion Iran war request.
S20261105-04.t: A Democratic Congress changes the terms of US policy toward Türkiye as well as Iran and Israel.

S20261105-05.h: Trump says no immediate Iran strike plan, but Washington is split on escalation
S20261105-05.s: Trump said there is no immediate plan to strike Iran, though US forces are 'locked and loaded'. He warned of a 'heavy hit' and said he can end the operation when he chooses. Reports describe disagreement among officials over escalation versus a negotiated exit, and analysts say the midterm result leaves him with few good options.
S20261105-05.t: Whether the US escalates or negotiates an exit decides how much regional spillover Türkiye faces.

S20261105-06.h: Mojtaba Khamenei warns of wider response and says US hostility will persist
S20261105-06.s: Iran's Supreme Leader said US hostility will continue whichever party controls Congress. He laid out a doctrine of immediate responses with no geographic limit to any renewed attack. He cited Hormuz management and strikes on US bases as a response that could widen.
S20261105-06.t: A declared unlimited-geography response doctrine raises the risk of regional escalation next to Türkiye.

S20261105-07.h: Iranian officials threaten retaliation, including on European bases, if attacked
S20261105-07.s: IRGC and government figures warned that Iran would drop proportional retaliation and target enemy leaders and assets if attacked. An Iranian MP told Euronews that bases in Italy and Germany would be fired on if used by the US. Berlin says it is working with regional states to prevent renewed attacks, and Iran rebuked the German foreign minister.
S20261105-07.t: Threats against NATO-hosted bases and a proxy front reaching Bab al-Mandab bring the conflict close to Türkiye's alliance and neighbourhood.

S20261105-08.h: Iranian leaders hail US midterm result as rejection of Trump's war
S20261105-08.s: Iranian officials, including negotiator Ghalibaf, said Americans voted 'no to war' and warned Washington against betraying that will. Tehran nonetheless stayed on alert for renewed strikes. Domestic debate asks whether US policy will change.

S20261105-09.h: IRGC claims it shot down US drones over Qeshm and Hormuz
S20261105-09.s: The IRGC claimed its air defences downed a US MQ-1 over Qeshm Island, its 15th such aircraft, and an MQ-9 over the Strait. IRNA cites a 56th MQ-9 downed. A factbox describes Qeshm's military facilities and its role in controlling Hormuz traffic amid reports it is a US target.

S20261105-10.h: Oil falls toward $100 as traders bet on easing of Iran war
S20261105-10.s: Brent fell for a third session toward or below $100, with one report putting it near $94. Markets reacted to Democratic gains and Trump ruling out immediate strikes. Gulf markets gained.
S20261105-10.t: Lower oil prices ease Türkiye's energy import bill.

S20261105-11.h: Iran calls US reply on Hormuz plan unconvincing; seeks Chinese and Russian backing
S20261105-11.s: Iran called the US response to its Hormuz plan unconvincing while indirect talks continue, and Trump confirmed US strikes on an Iranian anti-aircraft site. Iran is seeking China and Russia's backing, and mediators are weighing a Chinese guarantee of US sanctions relief.

S20261105-12.h: Pakistan's Sharif calls Tehran talks with Saudi and Turkish officials positive
S20261105-12.s: Sharif said talks in Tehran with Pakistani, Iranian, Saudi and Turkish officials were positive for restoring regional peace. Egypt's Sisi urged Trump and Iran to show flexibility, and Saudi Arabia, Qatar and Egypt are pursuing diplomacy.
S20261105-12.t: Türkiye is a participant in the mediation track alongside Pakistan and Saudi Arabia.

S20261105-13.h: US sanctions Turkish and Indian entities over Iranian oil sales
S20261105-13.s: The US Treasury sanctioned companies and individuals in India and Türkiye under Operation Economic Outcast for aiding Iran's oil trade, including an India-based shipping network. The State Department also sanctioned two individuals and a Nigeria-based firm for allegedly supplying Iran with MANPADS.
S20261105-13.t: Turkish firms are directly exposed to US secondary sanctions tied to Iran.

S20261105-14.h: Iran strikes Kurdish opposition groups in Iraq's Kurdistan Region
S20261105-14.s: Iran struck the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, targeting Kurdish opposition groups, after the US midterm elections.
S20261105-14.t: Iranian strikes on Kurdish groups in northern Iraq affect the security environment on Türkiye's border.

S20261105-15.h: Houthis hit Saudi Arabia, claiming Riyadh airport strike; Saudi air defences active
S20261105-15.s: The Houthis claimed a ballistic missile strike on Riyadh airport and four attacks on Saudi forces. They urged airlines to avoid Saudi airspace. A coalition force destroyed three drones, and another Indian national died in the Riyadh airport attack, taking the regional toll to 24.
S20261105-15.t: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia raise the stakes of the Mecca defence pact Türkiye is ratifying.

S20261105-16.h: Yemeni government forces claim gains against Houthis as Taiz stays besieged
S20261105-16.s: The Yemeni army says it seized Houthi positions in al-Jawf, gained ground in Taiz and killed about 340 fighters. The Giants Brigades destroyed three launchers. Houthis have blockaded Taiz for a month, and the Red Cross delivered medical supplies.

S20261105-17.h: Al-Sharaa visits Riyadh; Saudi Arabia and Syria sign defence and development deals
S20261105-17.s: Syria's president met Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman on his second visit in weeks. The two sides signed a defence ministries cooperation agreement and memorandums covering infrastructure and energy, plus $403.6 million in development financing.
S20261105-17.t: Saudi military and financial ties with Damascus compete with Türkiye's own influence in Syria.

S20261105-18.h: EU enlargement report criticises Türkiye; Ankara rejects it as biased
S20261105-18.s: The Commission says Türkiye's democratic decline is widening its gap with EU standards and urged normalisation with Cyprus. Marta Kos called Türkiye a strategic partner, and the report notes Ankara's regional role. The Foreign Ministry rejected the report as double standards and backing unrealistic Greek and Greek Cypriot positions.
S20261105-18.t: Accession remains frozen, with Cyprus and rights criticism hardening positions on both sides.

S20261105-19.h: Cyprus talks: Holguin meets Erhürman as Fidan expected in north; Ustel urges two states
S20261105-19.s: UN envoy Holguin met Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman, and Fidan is reportedly due in the north on Friday. Nicosia criticised a publicised meeting with a Turkish representative. Erhürman accused Christodoulides of using his 19 proposals to sideline Guterres's seven-point plan, while Ustel called for two-state recognition.
S20261105-19.t: The Cyprus track is being contested at the same moment as the EU report's criticism of Ankara.

S20261105-20.h: Erdoğan visits South Korea to deepen strategic ties
S20261105-20.s: Erdoğan made a three-day visit to South Korea, his first in eight years, at the invitation of President Lee Jae Myung. The sides are moving to institutionalise ties ahead of the 70th anniversary of relations in 2027.
S20261105-20.t: Seoul is a partner for defence industry and Eurasian connectivity.

S20261105-21.h: Baykar tests TB2 launching Skydagger FPV kamikaze drones
S20261105-21.s: A Bayraktar TB2 released two Skydagger FPV drones in a strike test, acting as their communications relay. Selçuk Bayraktar also announced a firing test of 16 FPV drones launched from under a TB2.
S20261105-21.t: Mother-ship drone swarms extend Türkiye's export-led drone edge.

S20261105-22.h: Investment fund scandal: prosecutors summon ex-minister, charge journalists
S20261105-22.s: Istanbul prosecutors again summoned ex-minister Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya, her husband and ex-SPK chief Gönül as suspects. Journalists including Ağırel and Saymaz have been indicted over fund coverage, and AKP-MHP lawmakers rejected another inquiry bid. The FT calls the $20 billion crisis a Ponzi-to-Ponzi scheme affecting over 455,000 investors.
S20261105-22.t: The scandal is a domestic political and press-freedom test for the government.

S20261105-23.h: DEM Party and supporters demand release of Demirtaş on arrest anniversary
S20261105-23.s: DEM co-chair Hatimoğulları called for the immediate release of Demirtaş and Yüksekdağ after visiting him. Supporters issued a statement on the 10th anniversary of his arrest, and a court merged his Diyarbakır case with the Mersin case.
S20261105-23.t: Demirtaş's detention is a test for the process to end PKK violence.

S20261105-24.h: Kurdistan Parliament reactivated with new presidency after two-year deadlock
S20261105-24.s: The parliament elected Vala Fardi as speaker, Rami Nouri as deputy and Mona Qahwachi as secretary. The KDP and the region's president welcomed the move, while the PUK and New Generation boycotted.
S20261105-24.t: Functioning Iraqi Kurdish institutions matter to Ankara's relations with Erbil.

S20261105-25.h: US Democratic Congress may complicate Erdoğan's sanctions relief and fighter jet goals
S20261105-25.s: Former Turkish diplomats say Democratic control of both chambers could complicate Erdoğan's efforts to win sanctions relief and advanced US fighter jets.
S20261105-25.t: Congress is the main obstacle to F-35/F-16 access and CAATSA relief.

S20261105-26.h: Israel certifies election results; Herzog opens coalition talks
S20261105-26.s: The election commission confirmed final results that cost Netanyahu's coalition its majority and found no fraud. Herzog began consultations, with Eisenkot leading endorsements, including from Raam, while the Religious Zionists and Shas back Netanyahu. Shas lost nearly half its seats and Deri asked to step down. A government must be formed within 13 weeks or early elections follow.
S20261105-26.t: A government without Netanyahu could change Israeli policy on Syria and Gaza, which affects Türkiye.

S20261105-27.h: Netanyahu alleges foreign interference as Shin Bet chief faces criticism
S20261105-27.s: Netanyahu alleged foreign interference and called for an investigation. Haaretz reports he and Shin Bet chief Zini are moving to undermine the results, risking a constitutional crisis. Ben-Gvir urged arrests of Arab party leaders, a journalist was arrested, and former security officials criticised Zini for demanding probes without evidence.

S20261105-28.h: Israeli opposition cites US midterms as grounds to remove Netanyahu
S20261105-28.s: Lapid, Golan and other rivals said Democratic control of Congress shows Netanyahu squandered bipartisan US support. Lapid ruled out a Netanyahu-led unity government, and Golan warned of sanctions and isolation. Right-wing politicians stayed largely silent.

S20261105-29.h: Trump says US will end military aid to Israel by December 2026
S20261105-29.s: Trump said he and Netanyahu agreed to end about $4 billion in annual US military aid. It prompted concern about a US retreat and about Gulf confidence in US commitments. Analysts say Israel may have to choose between interceptors and costly operations, and senator-elect El-Sayed backed the plan while seeking a weapons-sales ban.
S20261105-29.t: A shift in US-Israel ties alters the regional balance Ankara works within.

S20261105-30.h: Democratic win prompts reassessment of US support for Israel
S20261105-30.s: Analysts say Democratic control of Congress and Republican unease could bring the biggest reassessment of US support for Israel in decades, with more scrutiny of operations in Iran, Gaza and Lebanon. Eleven new lawmakers join advocates pushing to end military support. Israeli commentators say its standing is deteriorating.

S20261105-31.h: Israeli probe: Shin Bet and IDF knew Deif went underground before October 7
S20261105-31.s: A Haaretz report on an Israeli investigation says Shin Bet and the IDF knew Hamas military chief Deif had gone underground hours before the attack. Other reports say warnings about Gaza movement were judged routine.

S20261105-32.h: Israeli strikes and shelling continue in southern Lebanon despite ceasefire
S20261105-32.s: Lebanese state media report Israeli artillery shelling and home burnings in southern Lebanon. A drone strike on a motorcycle in Mercayun hit one person, and another strike killed one.

S20261105-33.h: Lebanese PM warns Hezbollah off another war; UN warns on peacekeeper withdrawal
S20261105-33.s: Lebanon's prime minister warned Hezbollah against joining another war. UN peacekeeping chief Lacroix warned that withdrawing peacekeepers from southern Lebanon risks a security vacuum.

S20261105-34.h: Israeli strikes kill Palestinians in Gaza despite ceasefire
S20261105-34.s: An Israeli drone hit a tent in Gaza, killing one, and strikes killed three in 24 hours. The IDF and Shin Bet said they killed six militants near Khan Yunis, and Israeli forces bombed displacement camps.

S20261105-35.h: Russian bombing of Komyshuvakha in Zaporizhzhia kills at least 40
S20261105-35.s: A Russian bomb struck a school or shelter and aid distribution site, killing 37 to 40 people, with dozens missing and the search in its third day. Kyiv says bodycam video shows a double-tap strike, and Israel condemned the attack.

S20261105-36.h: Russian strikes cause Kyiv's worst water outage and cut nuclear output
S20261105-36.s: A 310-drone overnight attack, with 272 downed, and strikes on substations caused Kyiv's worst water outage of the war. Ukrainian nuclear plants cut output because distribution was limited. Zelensky ordered faster repairs.

S20261105-37.h: Zelensky briefed ahead of Abu Dhabi trilateral talks with Russia
S20261105-37.s: Zelensky held a 90-minute call with Witkoff and Kushner on air defence, the drone deal and security guarantees. The Kremlin says the talks will focus on security guarantees and be closed-door, and Trump claims both sides are ready for a deal. Ukrainian negotiators reportedly dispute that.
S20261105-37.t: The talks are in the Gulf rather than Istanbul, bypassing Türkiye's mediation role.

S20261105-38.h: China confirms talks on possible Xi-Trump-Putin meeting at APEC
S20261105-38.s: China's foreign ministry said it is in communication with relevant parties on a possible trilateral meeting on the sidelines of APEC in Shenzhen.

S20261105-39.h: Commission sets no Ukraine accession date as Moldova pulls ahead
S20261105-39.s: The Commission's report confirms Ukraine meets conditions to open remaining negotiating clusters but sets no membership date. Moldova is seen outpacing Ukraine, and Kyiv aims to start closing chapters in early 2027.

S20261105-40.h: Ukraine and Western partners meet in Brussels on recovery and 2027 funding
S20261105-40.s: Delegations from Ukraine, the EU, US, UK, France, Germany, NATO and the World Bank discussed the Prosperity Plan, reconstruction and 2027 funding. They also coordinated ahead of the Abu Dhabi talks. TASS says it ended without practical results.

S20261105-41.h: Zelensky in Madrid and with Pistorius seeks faster air defence deliveries
S20261105-41.s: Zelensky arrived in Spain for talks on air defence, defence cooperation and production. He also discussed with Pistorius accelerating PAC-2, IRIS-T and F-16 ammunition deliveries amid a chronic shortage.

S20261105-42.h: NABU detains senior SBU general; SBU chief dismisses officials
S20261105-42.s: Anti-corruption detectives detained SBU first deputy head Serhiy Duka and searched other senior SBU officials, with bodyguards allegedly threatening detectives. SBU chief Poklad dismissed two officials implicated in the Carthage probe, and NABU completed its Midas probe on Energoatom.

S20261105-43.h: Ukrainian intelligence: Russia stockpiled up to 700 ballistic missiles
S20261105-43.s: Military intelligence estimates Russia held up to 700 ballistic and several thousand cruise missiles as of October. It can produce over 200 missiles per month, including up to 110 ballistic.

S20261105-44.h: Israeli forces raid villages in Syria's Quneitra countryside
S20261105-44.s: Israeli forces shelled the Quneitra countryside and moved vehicles and tanks into Jaba al-Khashab, raiding homes and buildings. No casualties were reported.
S20261105-44.t: Israeli presence in southern Syria complicates Türkiye's Syria strategy.

S20261105-45.h: WSJ: NATO drafts plan for conventional strikes deep inside Russia
S20261105-45.s: The Wall Street Journal reports NATO is preparing a defence plan that envisions conventional strikes deep in Russian territory to disrupt supply lines.
S20261105-45.t: As a NATO member with a Black Sea role, Türkiye would be affected by a more offensive alliance posture toward Russia.

S20261106-01.h: Turkish parliament ratifies Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
S20261106-01.s: The Grand National Assembly approved the Mecca joint defence agreement by 279 votes to 119, after first approving its opening article. Under the pact an attack on one party is treated as an attack on all. Commentary says it opens the way to Turkish military support for Riyadh against the Houthis, though deploying troops needs separate parliamentary approval.
S20261106-01.t: Türkiye is now formally bound to a three-way collective defence pact that could draw it into the Saudi-Houthi conflict.

S20261106-02.h: Tankers and a tugboat burn in Strait of Hormuz amid mine claims
S20261106-02.s: Iran says several oil tankers and a tugboat caught fire in separate incidents east of Hormuz, and its navy says some hit naval mines. Tehran accuses the US of pushing ships along a mined route. UKMTO warns of rising attacks on shipping, and Gulf states are rattled.
S20261106-02.t: Disruption in Hormuz pushes up energy prices and raises Türkiye's import costs.

S20261106-03.h: Trump weighs renewed Iran strikes or a deal as Vance breaks ranks
S20261106-03.s: After Republican midterm losses, Trump is reportedly weighing fresh strikes against a deal, with Qatar mediating. Vance publicly blamed the Iran war for the defeat and reportedly urged agreement, while the CIA director and Treasury secretary urged keeping the blockade. US officials are described as divided.
S20261106-03.t: A US decision on escalation or settlement with Iran directly affects Türkiye's border security and energy exposure.

S20261106-04.h: Trump warns of destroying the rest of Iran, 'you'll know soon enough'
S20261106-04.s: Trump said the US may have to destroy the rest of Iran and that a decision on escalation will come soon, though he would prefer not to. Iran's parliament speaker Ghalibaf said the US is preparing the next phase of the war despite Vance's calls to end it.
S20261106-04.t: Renewed US strikes on Iran would raise risks along the Turkish border and for regional trade.

S20261106-05.h: Iran sends nuclear proposal via Qatar, keeps Hormuz closed pending demands
S20261106-05.s: Iran passed a new nuclear proposal to Washington through Qatar and says Hormuz stays closed until its sanctions and reparations demands are met. Tehran is debating whether to negotiate or keep pressure, while rejecting direct talks despite a Russian mediation offer. Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei is reportedly building a new decision-making system.
S20261106-05.t: A US-Iran deal or breakdown shapes Ankara's mediation role and regional stability.

S20261106-06.h: Araghchi works Gulf and regional phone diplomacy as Iran-US tension persists
S20261106-06.s: Iran's foreign minister spoke with counterparts from Oman, the UAE, Jordan, Saudi Arabia, Qatar, Pakistan and Cyprus. Egypt and Saudi Arabia urged diplomacy to avert renewed confrontation. Qatar is mediating over the US naval blockade.
S20261106-06.t: Regional diplomacy around Iran crowds the field in which Türkiye seeks a mediating role.

S20261106-07.h: Fidan and Araghchi discuss Iran-US negotiations by phone
S20261106-07.s: Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan phoned Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi to discuss the Iran-US negotiation process and regional developments.
S20261106-07.t: Ankara is positioning itself as an interlocutor with Tehran while seeking closer border security cooperation.

S20261106-08.h: Turkish soldier killed by gunfire from Iranian side of border
S20261106-08.s: A Turkish soldier was killed on the Iranian border in Hakkari on October 31, with gunfire believed to have come from the Iranian side. Ankara says it wants closer border security cooperation with Tehran.
S20261106-08.t: A Turkish fatality from Iranian-side fire tests Ankara's balancing between Tehran and its new Gulf alignment.

S20261106-09.h: IRGC says it downed or seized US MQM-170 drones over Qeshm
S20261106-09.s: The IRGC says it brought down two US MQM-170 reconnaissance drones over Qeshm Island using electronic warfare, and later said it seized them. The claims are not independently verified.

S20261106-10.h: Putin receives Iran's security chief Rezaei with message from Mojtaba Khamenei
S20261106-10.s: Putin met Mohsen Rezaei at the Kremlin, with intelligence chief Kostyukov present, and received a message from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. The meeting came as Iran seeks to end hostilities with the US and sought Russian support.
S20261106-10.t: Deeper Russia-Iran security ties alter the balance on Türkiye's eastern and Black Sea flanks.

S20261106-11.h: Russia reportedly to supply Iran 90 missile launchers; US sanctions air-defence aid
S20261106-11.s: The Financial Times reports Russia agreed to supply Iran 90 helicopter-mounted launchers for precision-guided missiles, alongside weapons and intelligence sharing. The US sanctioned three entities for aiding Iran's air defences and others over portable air-defence supplies.
S20261106-11.t: Russian arms flows to Iran raise the military stakes next door.

S20261106-12.h: US sanctions Indian and Turkish firms over fake ship registries for Iranian tankers
S20261106-12.s: The US Treasury sanctioned Indian and Turkish firms accused of faking ship registries to help Iranian tankers evade sanctions.
S20261106-12.t: Turkish firms face sanctions exposure that may strain Ankara-Washington ties.

S20261106-13.h: Hegseth faces impeachment push over Iran war after GOP midterm losses
S20261106-13.s: Rep. Thomas Massie plans to force a House vote to impeach Hegseth. Hegseth says he will not back down, and Trump backed him.

S20261106-14.h: Tanker hit by two projectiles north of Qatar
S20261106-14.s: Two unidentified projectiles struck a tanker about 50 nautical miles north of Madinat ash Shamal off Qatar. Crew status is unconfirmed.

S20261106-15.h: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missile fired at Medina
S20261106-15.s: The coalition says it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile aimed at Medina after a civil defence warning near Yanbu. It also downed a drone over eastern Saudi Arabia.
S20261106-15.t: Houthi fire on Saudi holy cities is the threat the new Mecca pact is meant to meet.

S20261106-16.h: Yemen war: Houthis demand $51bn as government offensive grinds on
S20261106-16.s: The WSJ reports Houthis demand $51 billion from Saudi Arabia and recognition as Yemen's ruler while advancing toward Aden. Yemen's government says it carried out over 40,000 strikes in a month, and the WHO reports 1,771 killed since August.
S20261106-16.t: The Yemen war is the front where Türkiye's new Saudi defence commitment could be tested.

S20261106-17.h: Saudi Arabia and Syria sign defence cooperation deal and loans
S20261106-17.s: During al-Sharaa's second Riyadh visit in under a month, the two states signed military and financial agreements, including $403m in loans. Reports say Syria considered aiding the fight against the Houthis.
S20261106-17.t: Saudi-Syrian military ties compete with Ankara's own influence in Damascus.

S20261106-18.h: Eisenkot set to get first chance to form Israeli government
S20261106-18.s: Arab-led parties and the Democrats recommended Gadi Eisenkot, giving him 67 of 120 recommendations against 46 for Netanyahu, after United Torah Judaism declined to back either. President Herzog is due to name his choice on Sunday.
S20261106-18.t: A change of government in Israel would affect Ankara's strained relations with Jerusalem.

S20261106-19.h: Israel, Greece and Cyprus reject Turkey-Libya maritime deal, form defence working group
S20261106-19.s: Meeting in Athens, the three states rejected the Turkey-Libya maritime deal and agreed to a trilateral defence industry working group and more maritime security cooperation.
S20261106-19.t: The bloc directly targets Türkiye's eastern Mediterranean maritime claims.

S20261106-20.h: Fidan to visit northern Cyprus as UN-hosted Cyprus talks gain momentum
S20261106-20.s: Fidan is expected in northern Cyprus to meet Turkish Cypriot leader Erhürman before a UN-confirmed trilateral meeting on November 9 with Christodoulides and envoy Holguín. Christodoulides says talks are moving positively.
S20261106-20.t: The talks bear on Ankara's two-state line and its leverage in the Cyprus question.

S20261106-21.h: Erdoğan seeks talks with Putin after meeting Zelenskyy
S20261106-21.s: After talks with Zelenskyy, Erdoğan said he wants to speak with Putin on ending the war and that Turkish officials are engaging both sides.
S20261106-21.t: Ankara reasserts its role as mediator in the Ukraine war.

S20261106-22.h: Erdoğan to visit Baku November 8 amid headscarf rift with Azerbaijan
S20261106-22.s: Erdoğan plans to visit Azerbaijan after Aliyev skipped a Turkic summit and a dispute over Baku's school headscarf restrictions.
S20261106-22.t: The visit aims to repair ties with Türkiye's closest regional ally.

S20261106-23.h: Russian strike on Komyshuvakha school kills at least 43
S20261106-23.s: The death toll from a Russian strike on a school and aid centre in Zaporizhzhia region rose to 43, with dozens possibly trapped. Ukrainian bodycam footage and independent investigators challenge Moscow's claim of a military target.

S20261106-24.h: Trump says Ukraine deal is close after meeting Putin's envoy
S20261106-24.s: Trump met a Russian envoy and said a Russia-Ukraine deal and a wider European security arrangement are close. Dmitriev said Putin values Trump's efforts. Melania Trump hosted Russian and Ukrainian officials on the Oleshky ceasefire ahead of Abu Dhabi talks.
S20261106-24.t: A US-Russia settlement on Ukraine and European security would reshape Türkiye's Black Sea and NATO environment.

S20261106-25.h: NATO hosts Brussels talks on Ukraine security guarantees; Meloni complains of EU disarray
S20261106-25.s: Ukrainian, US, French, UK, German and NATO officials met in Brussels on security guarantees, and the NATO-Ukraine Council held an extraordinary meeting. Italy's Meloni complained the EU lacks a single voice and called for a dedicated envoy.
S20261106-25.t: Post-war European security architecture will affect Türkiye's NATO role.

S20261106-26.h: Zelensky hopes Democratic Congress will lift US aid to Ukraine
S20261106-26.s: Zelensky said he hopes the midterm result brings stronger US financial and weapons support, though Washington has not delivered $16 billion promised earlier. Moscow says it relies on Trump to continue peace efforts.

S20261106-27.h: Ukrainian strikes cripple Russian refineries and Rostov ports
S20261106-27.s: Ukraine has reportedly knocked out 15 of Russia's 38 major refineries. Drones hit a Ryazan refinery overnight, and Rostov's three seaports are effectively halted.
S20261106-27.t: Disruption to Black Sea ports and Russian fuel exports touches Turkish trade and energy interests.

S20261106-28.h: EU releases €4.36bn to Ukraine; accession tensions persist
S20261106-28.s: The EU disbursed €4.36 billion, including macro-financial aid and defence funds. The Commission says Ukraine reached readiness in five chapters, while Hungary calls 2030 accession unrealistic and Germany pushes associate status.
S20261106-28.t: EU enlargement debates over Ukraine bear on Türkiye's own frozen accession.

S20261106-29.h: Poland detains six suspected of spying for Russia
S20261106-29.s: Poland detained five Polish nationals and a Russian woman accused of working for Russian intelligence and supplying military components.

S20261106-30.h: Bomb-hoax wave hits European flights; far-right Russian group claims some
S20261106-30.s: Hoax bomb threats diverted flights across Europe, and the EU activated aviation security information sharing. Russian extremists claimed threats against Aer Lingus and Finnair, though no hard link to Russia has been established.

S20261106-31.h: Talabani's PUK quits Kurdistan Regional Government
S20261106-31.s: PUK leader Bafel Talabani announced withdrawal from the KRG and non-recognition of its parliament's decisions, a rupture that could unravel the region. The EU welcomed the parliament's reactivation and urged government formation.
S20261106-31.t: Instability in the KRG affects Türkiye's border, energy and counter-PKK interests in northern Iraq.

S20261106-32.h: Türkiye's fund crisis probe widens with ex-minister jailed
S20261106-32.s: Former minister Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya was arrested in the fund investigation, and more political figures were summoned. The opposition demands answers, Şimşek faces resignation calls, and Türkiye has repaid $2.6bn to investors.
S20261106-32.t: The scandal is a domestic political and economic test for the government.

S20261106-33.h: Gunman kills eight in Afyonkarahisar attacks
S20261106-33.s: Eight people, including two teachers, were shot dead in a series of attacks in Afyonkarahisar. A suspect was reportedly arrested in Seyitgazi, Eskişehir, and motives are unclear.

S20261106-34.h: Türkiye unveils National Energy 2040 plan and nuclear targets
S20261106-34.s: Bayraktar set a 10,000 MW nuclear target by 2040 and meeting all oil and gas demand domestically, with large renewables investment. He said Akkuyu will enter operation within weeks.
S20261106-34.t: The plan targets energy security and lower import dependence.

S20261106-35.h: Türkiye and Qatar advance defence cooperation in Ankara
S20261106-35.s: Qatar's defence minister met Fidan and his Turkish counterpart in Ankara, and the defence industry chief discussed joint projects after the Badr pact signing. Turkish Interior Minister Çiftçi also met his Saudi counterpart.
S20261106-35.t: Gulf defence ties are expanding alongside the Saudi pact.

S20261106-36.h: Eurofighter eyes Turkish and Saudi orders; Aselsan unveils submarine mast
S20261106-36.s: Eurofighter is pursuing about 200 more aircraft, including 78 from Türkiye and Saudi Arabia. Aselsan developed the Mercan 100 submarine optronic mast.
S20261106-36.t: Both items concern Turkish air and naval modernisation.

S20261106-37.h: NATO launches counter-drone marketplace under Ankara Summit programme
S20261106-37.s: NATO created a marketplace to speed procurement of counter-drone systems under the Drone Edge programme agreed at the Ankara Summit. Allies committed over $40bn over five years.
S20261106-37.t: The programme stems from the Ankara Summit.

S20261106-38.h: PKK disarmament process advances as more members surrender
S20261106-38.s: Six more PKK members surrendered in the past week, per the Turkish Defence Ministry. Kurtulmuş says the Terror-Free Türkiye project will end terrorism, while DEM presses for parliamentary monitoring and prisoner releases.
S20261106-38.t: The process to end PKK violence remains the core of domestic security policy.

S20261106-39.h: Israeli fire continues in Gaza despite ceasefire; winter threat looms
S20261106-39.s: Israeli attacks killed several Palestinians despite the October ceasefire, with Gaza officials counting over 1,600 deaths since it began. Civil defence warned heavy rain threatens about 950,000 displaced people.

S20261106-40.h: Blair presses Gaza plan with Netanyahu and Herzog
S20261106-40.s: Tony Blair, for Trump's Board of Peace, met Netanyahu and Herzog to push Gaza demilitarisation and reconstruction, and will meet Eisenkot.
S20261106-40.t: Gaza arrangements bear on Türkiye's role and its standing with Hamas and Washington.

S20261106-41.h: Herzog warns of civil war as West Bank settler violence escalates
S20261106-41.s: Herzog warned Netanyahu and Katz that Jewish terrorism could spark civil war. Israel advanced settlement tenders and demolitions, while the UN cited 377 settler attacks since September.

S20261106-42.h: US-Israel aid strains: Trump halts $4bn as Israel faces funding gap
S20261106-42.s: Herzog said he was not told in advance of Trump's decision to halt $4bn in aid. Israel would need about $10bn after 2028 to cover existing orders, and US opinion has shifted after the midterms.
S20261106-42.t: A weaker US-Israel bond alters regional balances Ankara watches.

S20261106-43.h: Israeli forces raid and shell southern Syria
S20261106-43.s: Israeli forces carried out incursions and artillery fire in Daraa and Quneitra and fired shells near Beit Jinn.
S20261106-43.t: Israeli activity in southern Syria competes with Türkiye's interests in Syria.

S20261106-44.h: Oil prices swing as Iran war uncertainty and rate hikes weigh
S20261106-44.s: Oil rebounded from a two-month low on Hormuz fears. The Bank of England raised rates and warned of more if the conflict continues, and Russia's oil revenues more than doubled.
S20261106-44.t: Energy prices and global rate rises affect Türkiye's import bill and inflation.

S20261106-45.h: South Korea to extend anti-piracy patrols toward Hormuz
S20261106-45.s: Seoul plans to extend its Cheonghae unit's patrols toward Oman's Duqm under US pressure, while staying out of the Iran war.

S20261107-01.h: Trump weighs resuming war on Iran as soon as November 9
S20261107-01.s: Reports citing Fox News and others say Trump is considering new strikes on Iran on November 9. Trump says he has not decided and may strike again. US officials reportedly told Gulf allies to prepare, while Israeli media say the IDF is ready but no major US buildup has been detected.
S20261107-01.t: A renewed US-Iran war would hit Türkiye's border region, energy prices and Hormuz trade, and would test the new Mecca defence pact.

S20261107-02.h: Iran claims more US drones downed over Qeshm Island amid reported strikes
S20261107-02.s: Iran's army and IRGC say air defences shot down US MQ-9 and MQ-1 drones over Qeshm Island, and the IRGC claims 72 drones in total. Iranian media reported two projectiles or missiles hitting the Suza area and explosions near Qeshm and Bandar Khamir. Trump said US forces attacked Iranian air defence systems without saying when.
S20261107-02.t: Escalation around Hormuz threatens Turkish trade and energy supplies and raises the risk of spillover into Iraq.

S20261107-03.h: Iran sends nuclear proposal to US via Qatar
S20261107-03.s: Iran reportedly sent Washington a nuclear proposal through Qatar, conditional on the US first meeting Tehran's seven demands. Bloomberg says the sides moved closer, and Trump says Iran cannot act on its nuclear programme without US approval. Highly enriched uranium and inspector access remain the sticking points.
S20261107-03.t: A deal would lower the regional war risk that endangers Turkish energy, trade and border security.

S20261107-04.h: Trump says US-Iran talks continue; Vance reportedly ran indirect channel
S20261107-04.s: Trump said the US is talking to Iran, is doing very well and has beaten Iran, and he sees progress. Reports say JD Vance has held indirect talks for two weeks on a new ceasefire and restarting nuclear negotiations. Trump also reiterated that the US controls Hormuz shipping.

S20261107-05.h: Qatari emir and Trump discuss de-escalation; Doha denies PM said talks failed
S20261107-05.s: Qatar's emir and Trump discussed Qatari mediation, navigation freedom and energy security. Qatar rejected reports that its prime minister said no US-Iran agreement had been reached. The prime minister had urged both sides not to wait for a perfect moment.
