S20261107-05.t: Qatar is a close Turkish partner and its mediation shapes whether Ankara faces a wider Gulf war.

S20261107-06.h: Iran says it will no longer accept US paper commitments
S20261107-06.s: SNSC deputy secretary Ali Bagheri said Tehran will not rely on written US commitments after repeated breaches over 18 months and four derailed rounds of talks. He said Washington must take concrete steps before new negotiations.

S20261107-07.h: Iran sets seven conditions for reopening Hormuz, grants selective passage
S20261107-07.s: Iran's army spokesman said the US must accept seven conditions before Hormuz reopens. Tehran says ships from India, China, Qatar and Iraq may pass freely, which analysts call politically risky. Former minister Mottaki said the IRGC Navy disables several ships daily and urged the US to lift its blockade before talks.
S20261107-07.t: Selective passage and a continued blockade disrupt Turkish shipping and energy imports via the Gulf.

S20261107-08.h: IRGC says two tankers using unauthorised Hormuz routes hit mines
S20261107-08.s: The IRGC Navy said two oil tankers struck mines and caught fire while using unauthorised routes near the Strait of Hormuz.

S20261107-09.h: Seafarer killed in apparent missile strike on tanker off Bahrain
S20261107-09.s: A seafarer died in an apparent missile attack on the Greek-owned tanker Velos Sapphire near Bahrain's Sitra port. UKMTO also reported an explosion near the waterline of a tanker off Oman. The UN maritime agency says 25 sailors have died in Hormuz-area attacks since February 28.

S20261107-10.h: Iran-linked ships looped over Gulf of Oman undersea cables after threats
S20261107-10.s: The FT reports Iran-linked ships went dark and looped over undersea internet cables in the Gulf of Oman after Tehran threatened regional digital infrastructure.

S20261107-11.h: Rezaei carries Khamenei letter to Putin, reportedly seeks S-400s
S20261107-11.s: Iran's security chief Mohsen Rezaei met Putin in Moscow for about three hours and delivered a message from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei. The Telegraph says it requests S-400 air defences, and other reports mention advanced air defence talks and a pipeline for Russian gas. Iran is also turning to Russia for gas ahead of winter.
S20261107-11.t: Deeper Russia-Iran military ties complicate Ankara's balancing between both neighbours.

S20261107-12.h: FT: Iran ordered 90 Russian missile launch systems in 2024-25
S20261107-12.s: The Financial Times reports Iran ordered 90 missile launch systems from Russian manufacturers, and Al Jazeera describes a rocket launcher deal as a sign of deepening Russia-Iran military ties.

S20261107-13.h: Iran warns of decisive response if US attacks again
S20261107-13.s: Iran's army, an MP and an IRGC adviser warned of a decisive response to renewed US attack despite a reported US naval pullback. One lawmaker said Europe could be put within missile range and oil could exceed $150.

S20261107-14.h: Iraq proposes regional mission to Tehran and Washington
S20261107-14.s: Iraq proposed a regional diplomatic mission to Iran and the US. Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein discussed it with Araghchi as Tehran outlined a plan to resume talks and reopen Hormuz. Baghdad is preparing emergency plans and urging armed groups not to join Iranian retaliation.
S20261107-14.t: Türkiye's southern neighbour Iraq risks being drawn into a US-Iran war.

S20261107-15.h: Satellite images show Iran building near missile bases
S20261107-15.s: BBC Verify satellite imagery shows digging and new construction near Iranian missile bases and repairs of sites hit by US and Israeli strikes.

S20261107-16.h: Gulf states and Egypt press Iran for de-escalation
S20261107-16.s: Iran launched a diplomatic push towards Russia and the UAE. The UAE and Saudi foreign ministers and Egypt's foreign minister spoke with Iranian counterparts, while Araghchi called regional counterparts about easing tensions.

S20261107-17.h: Bahrain cracks down on Shi'ite clerics accused of loyalty to Tehran
S20261107-17.s: Bahrain launched a crackdown on Shi'ite clerics it accuses of allegiance to Tehran, after Iranian attacks on the country.

S20261107-18.h: US and Canada sanction eight money service firms over Iran links
S20261107-18.s: The US Treasury sanctioned eight Canada-based money services businesses, cutting them off from the dollar system, for alleged Iranian sanctions evasion, including links to narcotrafficker Ryan Wedding.

S20261107-19.h: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme
S20261107-19.s: The State Department's Rewards for Justice programme offered up to $20 million and possible relocation for intelligence on Iran's nuclear programme, as Trump says Tehran wants a deal.

S20261107-20.h: US midterm losses reshape Iran war politics
S20261107-20.s: Analysts and Iranian officials link the Democratic midterm gains to voter anger over the Iran war and prices, and expect scrutiny of war spending. Hegseth defended the war amid calls for his removal, and Trump replaced Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff.

S20261107-21.h: Turkish parliament ratifies Mecca defence pact with Saudi Arabia and Pakistan
S20261107-21.s: Parliament approved the Mecca mutual defence agreement despite opposition warnings it could draw Ankara into regional conflicts. Hakan Fidan says it is open to regional states that share a peace vision. Saudi and Turkish officials are also seeking closer security cooperation.
S20261107-21.t: The pact creates a trilateral military framework and raises Türkiye's regional obligations.

S20261107-22.h: Saudi Arabia and Syria sign defence pact; Syrian trainers head to Riyadh
S20261107-22.s: Saudi Arabia signed its first defence agreement with Syria's new leadership in Riyadh on Nov. 6, covering training and intelligence against the Houthis. Syrian advisers and a limited number of personnel are reportedly going to Saudi Arabia. Washington warned Damascus against regional entanglement.
S20261107-22.t: Syria's tie-up with Riyadh shifts Gulf-Syria alignments where Türkiye is also a key backer of Damascus.

S20261107-23.h: Houthi missile kills 12 at Riyadh airport; Saudi coalition intercepts more
S20261107-23.s: A Houthi missile killed at least 12 people at Riyadh's main airport. The Saudi-led coalition reported downing drones over Riyadh and Makkah and intercepting two ballistic missiles over Najran. Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain and Jordan condemned an attempted strike on Madinah.
S20261107-23.t: Houthi escalation against Saudi Arabia bears on Türkiye's new defence pact with Riyadh.

S20261107-24.h: Houthi missile hits Taiz market as Yemeni forces advance
S20261107-24.s: A ballistic missile strike on a Taiz market killed dozens of civilians, with the Yemeni government and Houthis blaming each other. The Yemeni army says it recaptured areas of Taiz.

S20261107-25.h: Pashinyan: Armenia and Türkiye to establish diplomatic relations soon
S20261107-25.s: Armenian PM Pashinyan said diplomatic relations will be established soon on the basis of mutual recognition of borders.
S20261107-25.t: Normalisation with Yerevan would open a Caucasus corridor and strengthen Ankara's regional standing.

S20261107-26.h: Fidan visits northern Cyprus, backs two-state solution as UN talks near
S20261107-26.s: Fidan met Turkish Cypriot leader Tufan Erhürman and said a two-state solution is the most realistic option. Cyprus condemned the visit as illegal. An enlarged meeting with guarantor powers is planned, and leaders meet UN envoy Holguín on Monday.
S20261107-26.t: Ankara hardens its Cyprus line just as the UN seeks to restart negotiations.

S20261107-27.h: Türkiye challenges Cyprus Navtex and French research vessel in east Mediterranean
S20261107-27.s: Türkiye issued a counter-Navtex against Greek and Cypriot seabed survey notices on the Crete-Cyprus route. Its Foreign Ministry also said a French-flagged vessel's planned research on Turkish-claimed continental shelf lacks Turkish approval.
S20261107-27.t: The cable-route surveys and the French vessel put Türkiye's continental shelf claims in direct contest with Greece, Cyprus and France.

S20261107-28.h: Kurtulmuş announces parliamentary committee on PKK peace process
S20261107-28.s: Speaker Numan Kurtulmuş announced a special parliamentary committee to oversee the process. He said the 'Terror-Free Türkiye' process is advancing and Türkiye will prevent provocations.
S20261107-28.t: The committee gives the disarmament process an institutional and legal track.

S20261107-29.h: Turkish fund crisis probe jails former minister Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya
S20261107-29.s: A court jailed former AKP minister Fatma Betül Sayan Kaya in the fund crisis investigation. Vice President Yılmaz said a payment is being prepared for next Friday from TMSF holdings. Detentions continue in the Şile case, and the Gaziosmanpaşa mayor was put under house arrest.
S20261107-29.t: The scandal reaches the ruling party's own ranks.

S20261107-30.h: Türkiye's UN Secretary-General candidate Sinirlioğlu outlines his goals
S20261107-30.s: Feridun Sinirlioğlu pledged a more just world and called for an experienced mediator. He said he would back real efforts toward a negotiated settlement in Ukraine.
S20261107-30.t: The candidacy would raise Türkiye's diplomatic profile at the UN.

S20261107-31.h: Türkiye unveils $500bn energy plan days before COP31 in Antalya
S20261107-31.s: The National Energy Plan targets self-sufficiency by 2040 through electrification, with no coal exit date. COP31 opens in Antalya on November 9, with disputes over climate finance and fossil fuels, and Amnesty urges attention to Türkiye's rights record.
S20261107-31.t: Türkiye hosts COP31 while trying to show an energy security agenda without a coal phase-out date.

S20261107-32.h: Türkiye's defence and aerospace exports reach $10 billion
S20261107-32.s: Defence and aerospace exports more than quadrupled in five years to $10bn in 2025 and rose 20.2% in the first ten months of 2026.
S20261107-32.t: Export growth strengthens the defence industry's strategic and economic weight.

S20261107-33.h: Bayraktar: Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline poses no threat to Türkiye
S20261107-33.s: Türkiye's energy minister and Iraq's energy minister said reactivating the Iraq-Syria pipeline is no economic threat to Türkiye.
S20261107-33.t: A Syria-Iraq export route could compete with the Iraq-Türkiye pipeline.

S20261107-34.h: Erdoğan says Gaza peace agreement is not being implemented
S20261107-34.s: Erdoğan said the Gaza peace agreement, which Türkiye helped sign, is not being implemented. He called the situation genocide and accused global institutions of standing by.
S20261107-34.t: Ankara signals frustration with the Gaza framework it guaranteed.

S20261107-35.h: Türkiye keeps buying Russian gas but eyes discount
S20261107-35.s: Bayraktar said Türkiye will keep buying Russian gas despite high prices, while volumes are falling. Analysts see Turkish complaints about price as a bargaining signal to Moscow.
S20261107-35.t: Ankara is using price talks to gain leverage with Moscow.

S20261107-36.h: PUK leader Talabani withdraws party from Kurdistan Regional Government
S20261107-36.s: Bafel Talabani announced the PUK's exit from the KRG after parliament's reactivation, accusing the KDP of undermining democracy.
S20261107-36.t: A split in Iraqi Kurdish government complicates Ankara's dealings in northern Iraq.

S20261107-37.h: Trump halts US military aid to Israel; Netanyahu's office reframes as partnership
S20261107-37.s: Netanyahu's office confirmed about $4bn in US military aid will be cut, framing the change as a move to partnership. Analysts say this exceeds Israeli expectations and could affect acquisition timelines for F-35, F-15 and Apache.
S20261107-37.t: Reduced US support changes Israel's regional posture and its leverage over Washington.

S20261107-38.h: Eisenkot gains momentum to form Israeli government after Lieberman lifts veto
S20261107-38.s: Opposition leader Eisenkot reports 67 backers as Lieberman lifted his veto on ultra-Orthodox parties. President Herzog will name a candidate on Sunday, and Arab parties have backed Eisenkot. Netanyahu's opponents accuse him of plotting a coup.
S20261107-38.t: A change of government would reshape Israeli policy toward Türkiye, Syria and Iran.

S20261107-39.h: Settlers seize Jericho homes with IDF commander's reported coordination
S20261107-39.s: Settlers seized eight properties in Jericho and displaced dozens of Palestinians. Haaretz sources say IDF Central Command's chief coordinated the entry while field commanders were not informed.

S20261107-40.h: Israel prepares for renewed Lebanon fighting as Lebanese fear escalation
S20261107-40.s: Yedioth Ahronoth reports the IDF is preparing for renewed fighting in Lebanon if war with Iran resumes. Lebanese residents are stocking up, and experts fear a US-Iran war could spread to Lebanon.

S20261107-41.h: Israeli forces shell villages in southern Syria
S20261107-41.s: Israeli troops shelled villages and farmland in Quneitra and advanced towards al-Hurriyeh, injuring several people according to local authorities.
S20261107-41.t: Israeli activity in southern Syria constrains Türkiye's role in Syria.

S20261107-42.h: Abu Dhabi trilateral talks on Ukraine set for November 10-11
S20261107-42.s: US, Russian and Ukrainian delegations meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday and Wednesday, the first such round since February. Putin discussed it with his Security Council, and Kyiv expects no breakthrough. Reports conflict on whether Budanov or Umerov will lead Ukraine's delegation.
S20261107-42.t: Türkiye has offered itself as a venue and mediator, so talks elsewhere reduce its role.

S20261107-43.h: Trump meets Dmitriev, touts 'big beautiful' deal covering all Europe
S20261107-43.s: Trump held a closed meeting with Putin's envoy Kirill Dmitriev and says a deal could involve all of Europe, not only Ukraine. He also agreed with Merz that the war must end soon and that NATO partners must approve any deal.
S20261107-43.t: A US-Russia deal reaching beyond Ukraine would reshape Black Sea and NATO security.

S20261107-44.h: Europe resists Kushner plan to rewrite European security architecture
S20261107-44.s: Kushner is pushing a US-led plan for a new security architecture with Russia, and Kallas rejects any Putin veto. European capitals fear exclusion and a link to a December review of US troop levels. They are also divided over who should negotiate with Moscow.
S20261107-44.t: A new European security order negotiated without Europeans would affect NATO's southern flank and Black Sea balance.

S20261107-45.h: Russia hits Kyiv with ballistic missiles as Zelensky warns of energy strikes
S20261107-45.s: Russia fired a wave of ballistic missiles at Kyiv after Zelensky warned of a mass attack on energy, Dnipro bridges and civilian infrastructure. Strikes damaged energy sites, cutting power and water in Kyiv and leaving emergency cuts in seven regions.

S20261107-46.h: Death toll in Komyshuvakha strike reaches 53
S20261107-46.s: Rescuers have recovered 53 bodies after a November 2 Russian strike on an aid centre and school in Zaporizhzhia Oblast, the deadliest Russian attack on that oblast since the full invasion.

S20261107-47.h: Ukrainian drones hit Russian refineries and depots
S20261107-47.s: Drones set the Afipsky refinery ablaze and caused explosions across southern Russia. Ukraine's General Staff says it hit ammunition depots in occupied Zaporizhzhia, and Zelensky says refinery strikes will continue.

S20261108-01.h: US carries out new limited strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island air defences
S20261108-01.s: Trump confirmed 'minor strikes' on an Iranian air defence system on Qeshm Island, days after an earlier attack, and said it is 'not a war'. Iranian media reported blasts on Qeshm and at Jask, Sirik and Bandar Abbas, though some Iranian outlets said the explosions were not an attack. Trump claimed progress in talks while mediators try to prevent escalation, and an IRGC militiaman was reported killed in Hormuz.
S20261108-01.t: Renewed US-Iran fighting near Hormuz threatens Türkiye's energy and trade exposure and its position as a would-be mediator.

S20261108-02.h: CENTCOM launches Task Force Iron Gate to cut Iran's land and Caspian supply routes
S20261108-02.s: US Central Command set up a Tampa-based task force to stop Iran moving weapons, sanctioned materials and illicit revenue over land borders and the Caspian Sea. It widens the naval blockade to land commerce, and reports say the US is preparing further expansion.
S20261108-02.t: Curbs on Iranian overland trade could pressure Türkiye and other neighbours that border Iran or sit on the Caspian corridors.

S20261108-03.h: US aircraft disable cargo ship M/V Huda in Gulf of Oman enforcing blockade
S20261108-03.s: CENTCOM said precision munitions disabled the St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda after its crew allegedly ignored warnings and tried to breach the blockade of Iran. The US released video of the strike, and UKMTO reported a military incident involving a cargo ship in the Gulf of Oman.
S20261108-03.t: Strikes on merchant shipping raise risks for Turkish-linked trade and insurance in the Gulf region.

S20261108-04.h: IRGC says two tankers hit mines near Strait of Hormuz
S20261108-04.s: The IRGC and Iran's navy said two tankers struck mines and caught fire in the eastern Hormuz area after entering a restricted zone, switching off navigation systems and taking an unauthorised route. Iranian outlets said warnings had been given.
S20261108-04.t: Mining incidents deepen the Hormuz disruption that feeds into Turkish energy costs and the economy.

S20261108-05.h: Iran's army says Hormuz stays closed until US accepts Tehran's conditions
S20261108-05.s: An Iranian army spokesperson said the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until Washington accepts Tehran's terms. This hardens Iran's position while mediators work on a deal.
S20261108-05.t: A prolonged closure keeps pressure on Turkish energy imports and Gulf trade.

S20261108-06.h: IRGC says limit on ballistic missile range has been lifted
S20261108-06.s: The IRGC announced Iran's self-imposed 2,000 km missile range limit no longer applies, allowing strikes on more distant targets if US or Israeli attacks resume. It did not say whether longer-range missiles exist.
S20261108-06.t: Longer-range Iranian missiles widen the threat envelope that includes Türkiye and NATO assets in the region.

S20261108-07.h: IRGC says it is building underground missile production sites, will unveil new weapons
S20261108-07.s: The IRGC spokesperson said new underground sites for weapons production and storage will keep missile output going under bombardment. He said new weapons will be unveiled if fighting with the US and Israel resumes.

S20261108-08.h: Iranian officials claim military is stronger and threaten devastating response
S20261108-08.s: Iran's army says it is stronger than at the start of the war in late February. Security council secretary Mohsen Rezaei warned Washington of a devastating response to any new attack and mocked Trump over the election, while an MP vowed consequences for Trump.

S20261108-09.h: Qatar says US-Iran mediation continues and Washington still wants a deal
S20261108-09.s: Qatar's prime minister said mediation is preventing regional escalation and the US remains willing to reach a deal. Qatar is reportedly pressing Tehran to admit UN nuclear inspectors, which could reopen Hormuz. Araghchi held calls with 12 counterparts urging regional security arrangements without outside interference.
S20261108-09.t: Türkiye backs diplomacy and could seek a role alongside Qatar in any settlement.

S20261108-10.h: Trump says US 'could be an occupier' in Iran, citing Hormuz control
S20261108-10.s: Trump acknowledged the limited Qeshm strikes and said the attacks may not be a war but an occupation, pointing to US control of the Strait of Hormuz.

S20261108-11.h: US offers $20 million reward for information on Iran's nuclear programme
S20261108-11.s: The State Department's Rewards for Justice offered up to $20 million and possible relocation for information on Iran's nuclear programme, citing lost IAEA continuity of knowledge. Treasury also sanctioned digital asset providers and Canadian money services firms over Iran-related transactions.

S20261108-12.h: After midterm losses, Vance and Bessent reportedly steer US toward ending Iran war
S20261108-12.s: Reports say Vance has taken direct control of Iran diplomacy and called for a swift end to the war, and Bessent is reaching out to China. NBC sources, however, say Trump's advisers see a two-month window for new Iran operations, and Trump has sent mixed signals on nuclear-site strikes.
S20261108-12.t: A US shift toward de-escalation matches Ankara's diplomatic line and eases regional risk.

S20261108-13.h: Report: Netanyahu and Mossad chief dropped pre-election Iran operation after US was tipped off
S20261108-13.s: Channel 12 reported Netanyahu and the Mossad chief planned an Iran operation before the election but halted it after an operative's error alerted Washington.

S20261108-14.h: Herzog tasks Eisenkot with forming Israel's next government; Netanyahu urges unity government
S20261108-14.s: After an inconclusive 27 October election, President Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot 28 days to form a coalition. Haaretz reports 67 lawmakers backed him against 46 for Netanyahu. Netanyahu called for a unity government and warned against a coalition reliant on Arab parties, and hundreds rallied for an inclusive government.
S20261108-14.t: A change of Israeli government could shift the tone of Israeli-Turkish relations and Israel's Syria policy.

S20261108-15.h: Trump announces end to US military aid to Israel, sparking bipartisan criticism
S20261108-15.s: Trump said roughly $4 billion in annual aid will end by year's end, timed around Michigan's election. Republicans and Democrats are criticising it, and analysts see eroding US support for Israel after the midterms.
S20261108-15.t: Weaker US-Israel ties could reduce Israel's room for manoeuvre in Syria and the eastern Mediterranean.

S20261108-16.h: Syrian troops reportedly deploying to Saudi Arabia and Yemen; Damascus denies
S20261108-16.s: Al-Monitor and Kurdistan24 reported thousands of Syrian troops deploying to Saudi Arabia and Yemen after a Saudi-Syrian defence deal. Damascus denied sending troops to Yemen, saying the deal focuses on training and could grow into mutual defence, with Saudi coordination visits starting in December.
S20261108-16.t: A Saudi-Syrian military axis changes the balance in post-Assad Syria, where Türkiye is the main external security partner.

S20261108-17.h: Houthis say Saudi airstrikes near Sanaa killed at least 22-33 people
S20261108-17.s: The Houthi-run health ministry reported varying tolls of 22 to 33 dead in Saudi strikes on a village near Sanaa. Riyadh has not commented and Reuters could not verify the figures.

S20261108-18.h: Houthi missiles and drones target Riyadh; Saudi-led coalition reports intercepts
S20261108-18.s: The Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a Houthi cruise missile launched toward Riyadh, and a drone was also intercepted. The Houthis claimed strikes on Riyadh airport, Aramco sites and a Najran National Guard camp, and the US Mission to the UAE warned of increased regional attack threats.

S20261108-19.h: Yemeni government forces report gains against Houthis as displacement rises
S20261108-19.s: Yemeni forces say they carried out over 800 operations against the Houthis and retook territory in Taiz and Lahij. Renewed fighting has displaced 313,000 people.

S20261108-20.h: Washington presses Baghdad to close Iran border crossings and curb armed groups
S20261108-20.s: Iraq's foreign minister said the US formally asked Baghdad to close most crossings with Iran, and that Hormuz losses reached about $60 billion. Washington reportedly warned it will target Iran-backed Iraqi groups in any new conflict, while envoy Tom Barrack discussed the Syria pipeline. Baghdad is investigating Gulf attacks launched from Iraqi territory.
S20261108-20.t: Iraq's squeeze affects Turkish trade and the Iraq-Türkiye energy and pipeline agenda.

S20261108-21.h: Iraqi PM cancels Mosul airport contracts tied to armed groups; Kataib Hezbollah hits back
S20261108-21.s: The Iraqi prime minister cancelled three companies' Mosul airport contracts over alleged armed-group links. Kataib Hezbollah accused him and an aide of amassing illicit wealth, and security forces seized a truck with 35 missiles near Baghdad.

S20261108-22.h: Israel keeps demolishing and shelling in south Lebanon, building military roads
S20261108-22.s: Lebanese state media report Israeli demolitions and shelling despite a framework agreement. Al Jazeera says Israel is building about 90 km of military roads and outposts across the south.

S20261108-23.h: Syrian intelligence says it foiled alleged Hezbollah plot, seizing explosives
S20261108-23.s: Syrian intelligence said it seized explosives and arrested two suspects allegedly tied to a Hezbollah plot, a day after a Lebanese delegation visited Damascus.

S20261108-24.h: Israeli forces re-enter Quneitra countryside, set up checkpoint
S20261108-24.s: Israeli forces entered the Quneitra countryside in southern Syria with 14 vehicles and set up a checkpoint searching passersby. Syrian media also reported troops storming a school.
S20261108-24.t: Continued Israeli encroachment in southern Syria adds to Ankara's concerns over Israel's role there.

S20261108-25.h: UN warns Gaza winter aid far short of needs as storms hit tents
S20261108-25.s: OCHA called for urgent entry of winter supplies and heavy machinery, citing funding gaps and Israeli restrictions. Gaza's death toll rose to 74,640, and storm collapses injured Palestinians in tents.

S20261108-26.h: Erdogan and Trump discuss Iran and Ukraine by phone
S20261108-26.s: Erdogan told Trump that Türkiye backs US-Iran diplomacy and will keep contributing to ending the war in Ukraine. They also discussed bilateral ties.
S20261108-26.t: Ankara positions itself as a diplomatic voice on both the Iran and Ukraine files.

S20261108-27.h: Egypt and Türkiye launch joint naval exercise in the Mediterranean
S20261108-27.s: Egypt and Türkiye began the Friendship Sea 2026 (Dostluk Denizi) naval exercise, which Türkiye's defence ministry also announced.
S20261108-27.t: The drill underlines Turkish-Egyptian rapprochement in the eastern Mediterranean.

S20261108-28.h: Fidan calls for global initiative to protect maritime chokepoints
S20261108-28.s: Foreign Minister Fidan said trade routes must be protected, shipping routes must not become war routes, and trade should be diversified amid Black Sea and Middle East disruptions.
S20261108-28.t: Ankara is framing itself as a champion of freedom of navigation as Hormuz and the Black Sea are disrupted.

S20261108-29.h: Şimşek says Gulf war will reshape region and Türkiye could benefit
S20261108-29.s: Finance Minister Şimşek said the war will fundamentally change the region, cut rivalry and boost cooperation, and Türkiye is likely to benefit. He also warned of energy supply shocks and urged diversified trade routes.
S20261108-29.t: Ankara sees the war as an opening to expand economic and energy roles.

S20261108-30.h: Turkish investment fund probe widens with new detentions and arrests
S20261108-30.s: Bulls Investment chairman Kemal Akkaya and former Takasbank manager Yunus Arıncı were detained again after release under judicial control. Four others including a former Capital Markets Board deputy chairman were jailed, and the AK Party promised new rules.
S20261108-30.t: The scandal weighs on domestic politics and investor confidence.

S20261108-31.h: Erdogan to visit Karabakh for Azerbaijan's Victory Day and meet Aliyev
S20261108-31.s: Erdogan will travel to Azerbaijan to attend Victory Day and hold talks with Ilham Aliyev on bilateral, regional and global issues.
S20261108-31.t: The visit reaffirms the Türkiye-Azerbaijan alliance and Caucasus agenda.

S20261108-32.h: Greece-Cyprus cable survey row: Fidan says dispute resolved as French vessel readies
S20261108-32.s: Fidan said the Navtex dispute over surveys for the Greece-Cyprus power cable was resolved, though Athens said Turkey's internal handling is no concern of Greece. The French vessel Abeille Marengo is set to start seabed surveys. Cyprus told the UN Turkish research ships are surveying its waters for a gas pipeline to the north.
S20261108-32.t: The cable and pipeline surveys keep the eastern Mediterranean maritime dispute with Greece and Cyprus live.

S20261108-33.h: UN envoy Holguin proposes Cyprus talks without preconditions
S20261108-33.s: Envoy Holguin proposed negotiations without preconditions and warned of huge damage if the current initiative fails. She postponed displaced-municipality meetings ahead of a Monday trilateral with the two leaders.
S20261108-33.t: The talks bear directly on Ankara's position on Cyprus.

S20261108-34.h: DEM Party urges concrete steps in PKK peace process
S20261108-34.s: DEM co-chair Tuncer Bakırhan urged the government to take concrete steps on the peace process, alongside the fund embezzlement and economic demands.
S20261108-34.t: Progress on the process to end PKK violence is a core domestic security matter.

S20261108-35.h: Iran says it shot down a US MQ-9 drone over Qeshm
S20261108-35.s: IRNA reported Iranian army air defences downed a US MQ-9 drone over Qeshm in the Strait of Hormuz. The US has not confirmed it in these items.

S20261108-36.h: Russia hits Kyiv region with 172 drones and 36 ballistic missiles
S20261108-36.s: The overnight attack hit energy facilities and the Northern Bridge, causing blackouts and water shortages. Zelensky said Russia likely used North Korean KN-23 missiles and Patriot shortages persist; Russia said it struck military-industrial, energy and transport targets.

S20261108-37.h: Russian strikes hit energy grid across Ukraine, including nuclear plant links
S20261108-37.s: Russian attacks damaged substations linking the Rivne and Khmelnytsky nuclear plants to Kyiv, and hit Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Chernihiv and a Naftogaz facility. Ukraine's energy minister said facilities were hit 18 times in 24 hours.

S20261108-38.h: Ukraine-US-Russia talks set for Abu Dhabi with Russian military delegation
S20261108-38.s: Russia will send a delegation led by a presidential aide, deputy foreign ministers including Ryabkov and military officers to trilateral talks, the first since February. Trump said he held several calls on ending the war, and Ukraine's foreign minister spoke to the UAE counterpart.
S20261108-38.t: Abu Dhabi hosting rather than Istanbul reflects competition for the mediator role Türkiye has sought.

S20261108-39.h: Europe fears US-Russia deal on European security; Zelensky warns it is dangerous
S20261108-39.s: Capitals fear a deal reportedly raised by Trump and envoy Kushner could weaken NATO and restore Russian influence. Zelensky said a 'big agreement' could be dangerous and that discussing post-war architecture before Ukraine's guarantees is risky. Moscow says Europeans have no place at the talks.
S20261108-39.t: A US-Russia understanding over European security would affect NATO cohesion and Black Sea balances.

S20261108-40.h: Ukraine strikes Rosneft Saratov refinery and Oryol defence plant
S20261108-40.s: Drones set fire to the Saratov refinery overnight, and Ukraine's General Staff said Neptune missiles hit the Proton-Electrotex plant in Oryol.

S20261108-41.h: Ukraine identifies Russian pilots behind Komyshuvakha school airstrike that killed 55
S20261108-41.s: Ukrainian military intelligence named a colonel and six pilots, and four Su-34 aircraft, allegedly responsible for the 2 November strike. The toll rose to 55.

S20261108-42.h: Germany says it cannot supply more Patriot systems to Ukraine
S20261108-42.s: Defence Minister Pistorius said new Patriot deliveries are impossible for now and urged other partners to step up air defence contributions.

S20261108-43.h: Shooting in Kraków's main square kills six; Tusk calls it terrorism
S20261108-43.s: A gunman killed six and wounded about a dozen in Kraków's Main Market Square near an anti-government demonstration. He was wounded and detained, and foreign nationals were among the victims.

S20261109-01.h: Three tankers burn in Strait of Hormuz; IRGC blames mines and unauthorised routes
S20261109-01.s: Iran's IRGC Navy and army navy say two to three tankers caught fire in or east of the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines on unauthorised routes. The IRGC warned ships against cooperating with US forces, and its spokesman said mines await in the strait. UKMTO reported two suspicious tanker incidents.
S20261109-01.t: Hormuz shipping risk drives up energy prices and import costs for Türkiye.

S20261109-02.h: US forces disable cargo ship M/V Huda trying to break Iran blockade
S20261109-02.s: CENTCOM said a US aircraft fired on and disabled the St. Kitts-flagged M/V Huda in the Gulf of Oman. The ship was leaving an Iranian port in breach of the US naval blockade, and its crew reportedly ignored warnings.
S20261109-02.t: Tightening blockade enforcement raises the risk of wider Gulf escalation that would hit Turkish trade and energy.

S20261109-03.h: Houthi attack damages Aramco tower in Riyadh financial district
S20261109-03.s: Debris from an attempted Houthi missile attack blew out windows across several floors of an Aramco building in the King Abdullah Financial District. The Saudi Energy Ministry said damage was minor with no casualties, and the Houthis claimed the attack.
S20261109-03.t: Attacks on Saudi energy assets add to Gulf instability and oil-price pressure that affects Türkiye.

S20261109-04.h: Iran threatens to 'rain down hell'; Araghchi gives US war-or-deal choice
S20261109-04.s: Foreign Minister Araghchi urged Washington to accept Iran's two-day proposal, demanding an end to the war on all fronts. He warned Iran would use its war option otherwise. Iran threatened to 'rain down hell' if the US escalates, and Trump said US forces are locked and loaded.
S20261109-04.t: A breakdown of US-Iran diplomacy would put Türkiye's border region and trade at risk.

S20261109-05.h: Trump says return to war with Iran unlikely if talks progress
S20261109-05.s: Trump told CNN renewed strikes on Iran are highly unlikely if Tehran signs a strong deal, with talks on the nuclear file and reopening Hormuz progressing. He noted three US carriers in the region. This follows weeks of rumours of US-Israeli strikes.
S20261109-05.t: A de-escalation track lowers regional spillover risk for Türkiye, though the outcome remains uncertain.

S20261109-06.h: US launches Task Force Iron Gate to cut Iran's land arms routes
S20261109-06.s: The US announced Task Force Iron Gate, which Trump said is in effect, to interdict Iranian arms flows across land borders and the Caspian Sea. Iran International notes northern routes may not be fully closed. An ex-Trump official says the land blockade undercuts Vance's Iran talks.
S20261109-06.t: Interdiction of land routes into Iran affects Türkiye's border transit and its Iran trade.

S20261109-07.h: Drone strike halts Khor Mor gas field, blacks out Iraqi Kurdistan
S20261109-07.s: A drone attack halted production at the Khor Mor gasfield, leaving over 70 percent of the Kurdistan Region without power. It cut national generation by about 2.8 GW. Iraq's prime minister ordered a joint investigation with the Kurdish authorities.
S20261109-07.t: Instability in the Kurdistan Region threatens Turkish energy and trade interests and the Kurdish political balance.

S20261109-08.h: Israel and US prepared Iran strike over weekend; Trump held off
S20261109-08.s: Israel and the US reportedly prepared a possible strike on Iran, but Trump held off while mediators pursued an agreement. Israeli analysts are weighing options including a broader offensive, negotiation or a limited strike.
S20261109-08.t: A renewed Israel-Iran war would raise regional security risks for Türkiye.

S20261109-09.h: Israel's Katz says mission against Iran is unfinished
S20261109-09.s: Defence Minister Israel Katz repeated that matters with Tehran are not finished and renewed his threat of new strikes on Iran.
S20261109-09.t: Israeli threats against Iran keep regional escalation risk high for Türkiye.

S20261109-10.h: Saudi-led coalition intercepts Houthi missiles and drone over Riyadh and Eastern Province
S20261109-10.s: The coalition said it intercepted ballistic and cruise missiles and a drone fired at Riyadh and the Eastern and Southern regions. Houthi spokesman Saria claimed a hit on Abqaiq. Saudi authorities issued shelter alerts, later lifted in some areas, and the coalition struck missile launchers.

S20261109-11.h: Houthis say Saudi-led strikes near Sanaa killed dozens
S20261109-11.s: The Houthis report 33 to 44 people killed and about 40 wounded in coalition air strikes around Sanaa. Reuters could not verify the figures. Iran's foreign ministry condemned the strikes and called for an end to the operations and the blockade.

S20261109-12.h: Report: Syrian troops deployed along Saudi-Yemen border; Damascus denies Yemen role
S20261109-12.s: A report citing Yemeni military sources claims hundreds of Syrian troops are deployed on both sides of the Saudi-Yemen border. Damascus reportedly denied sending troops to Yemen, is said to be weighing a defence pact covering Mecca, and condemned the Houthi attack on Aramco.
S20261109-12.t: Syria's possible alignment with Riyadh reshapes the Gulf-Syria balance in which Türkiye is also a player.

S20261109-13.h: Iran says no talks since 'shock' of US midterms
S20261109-13.s: Araghchi said there have been no negotiations with the US since the midterm elections and that Iran is waiting to resume them. A mediator trip is reportedly halted. Hardliners see Trump's electoral setback as a reason to demand a tougher deal.
S20261109-13.t: Türkiye, as a possible mediator, sees the diplomatic pause stall regional de-escalation.

S20261109-14.h: Rubio: no progress in Iran talks, demands unacceptable
S20261109-14.s: Secretary of State Rubio said the Iran talks have made little progress and called Tehran's demands outrageous. He said an agreement may not be possible but that Washington prefers diplomacy. He spoke ahead of a G7 meeting in France.

S20261109-15.h: Eisenkot tasked with forming Israeli government, open to Netanyahu's party joining
S20261109-15.s: President Herzog gave opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot the first chance to form a government after an inconclusive election. He has 28 days, and Ra'am and the Joint List say they will back him without joining the cabinet. Coalition partners disagree sharply.
S20261109-15.t: A post-Netanyahu government could change Israel's posture toward Türkiye and Syria.

S20261109-16.h: Türkiye and Iraq agree gradual Bashiqa handover and Sinjar security mechanism
S20261109-16.s: Türkiye and Iraq issued a joint statement on gradually handing the Bashiqa-Zilkan camp to Baghdad. They activated a joint security committee for Sinjar and reaffirmed ending the PKK presence there. The handover follows YBŞ disarmament.
S20261109-16.t: Consolidates Ankara's anti-PKK security gains in northern Iraq while reducing its military footprint.

S20261109-17.h: US asks Iraq to close all but two border crossings with Iran
S20261109-17.s: Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein said the US Treasury asked Baghdad to close all but two crossings with Iran as economic pressure on Tehran. He warned the step would also hurt Iraq. An Iraqi delegation also carried a US message to Tehran.
S20261109-17.t: Closer Iraq-Iran border controls shift regional trade flows that include Türkiye.

S20261109-18.h: Iraq reaches understandings with US to export oil via Hormuz Omani lane
S20261109-18.s: Iraq's foreign minister said Baghdad reached understandings with Washington to export oil through Hormuz via an Omani-side lane. He cited $60 billion in war losses.
S20261109-18.t: Alternative Iraqi export routes bear on the Iraq-Türkiye pipeline's role and regional oil flows.

S20261109-19.h: Explosions on Qeshm and near Bandar Abbas; Iran suggests not US attacks
S20261109-19.s: Iranian media reported four explosions on Qeshm Island, and blasts were also heard near Bandar Abbas, believed to be warning shots. Iran suggested the blasts were not US attacks.

S20261109-20.h: Trump says US has Iran targets including 38 bridges; claims Iran missile capacity cut
S20261109-20.s: Trump said the US has identified targets, including 38 bridges, in case strikes resume. He claimed Iran kept only 10% of missile and 15% of drone production capacity. He also said he could destroy Iran but is reluctant.

S20261109-21.h: Iran's IRGC dismisses Iron Gate as wordplay that will stay on paper
S20261109-21.s: The IRGC and Iranian officials dismissed the new US task force as wordplay and an ineffective economic pressure campaign. Iran also rejected the possibility of a US economic blockade of its land routes.

S20261109-22.h: Iran announces it has lifted self-imposed limit on missile range
S20261109-22.s: Iran said it has lifted its self-imposed limit on missile ranges, a move seen as a shift in its missile posture.
S20261109-22.t: Longer-range Iranian missiles widen the threat footprint around Türkiye.

S20261109-23.h: Iran-linked ships reportedly mapping and mining around undersea cables
S20261109-23.s: Reports say suspected Iran-linked ships are hovering over and mapping undersea telecom cables in the Gulf of Oman and placing mines. This follows Iranian threats to target cables in Hormuz.

S20261109-24.h: UAE rescues 22 crew from burning cargo ship in Gulf of Oman
S20261109-24.s: The UAE National Guard rescued 22 people from a cargo ship fire in the Gulf of Oman, amid the US blockade of Iran.

S20261109-25.h: Abu Dhabi Ukraine talks set for 10–11 November with European participation
S20261109-25.s: France's foreign minister said Europeans will take part in the US-mediated Russia-Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, without naming delegates. Ukraine named its negotiators, including Kirill Budanov. Peskov said Russia has held no security discussions with Europeans.
S20261109-25.t: Türkiye seeks a role in Ukraine diplomacy and Black Sea security, and Abu Dhabi talks sideline Istanbul.

S20261109-26.h: Russian strike on Komyshuvakha site kills 55; rescuers targeted
S20261109-26.s: A strike on an underground school and aid site in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, killed 55 people. A Russian FPV drone then hit rescue workers and equipment, and about 45 people remain missing.

S20261109-27.h: Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant loses external power, runs on diesel generators
S20261109-27.s: The plant lost its last external line after the Ferosplavna connection was damaged. Diesel generators carried the load until Ukrainian workers restored the line, after about ten hours. The IAEA called the safety situation precarious.

S20261109-28.h: Russian strikes cut power to up to 850,000 across Ukraine
S20261109-28.s: Overnight Russian strikes on energy infrastructure in Dnipropetrovsk, Kharkiv, Odesa and other regions left up to 850,000 people without power ahead of winter. Zelensky urged stronger EU sanctions.

S20261109-29.h: Kushner floats NATO-Russia Council model for European security architecture
S20261109-29.s: The Washington Post reports envoy Kushner proposed using the NATO-Russia Council as a model for new European security arrangements, alongside Ukraine ceasefire talks. European officials oppose the idea.
S20261109-29.t: A revived NATO-Russia format would change the Black Sea and NATO security balance Türkiye depends on.

S20261109-30.h: Russia says it struck ships carrying military cargo for Ukraine in Black Sea
S20261109-30.s: Russia's Defence Ministry said its forces hit three cargo ships carrying military goods and a container ship southwest of Odesa, and energy substations.
S20261109-30.t: Strikes on shipping in the Black Sea threaten Turkish maritime trade and Straits security.

S20261109-31.h: COP31 opens in Antalya under energy-security and US-absence shadow
S20261109-31.s: Türkiye hosts the UN climate conference for the first time, from 9 to 20 November, with about 190 countries. The US is absent, and critics note Türkiye's coal reliance. Ankara promotes electrification and zero-waste.
S20261109-31.t: A prestige diplomatic platform for Ankara, with scrutiny of its energy mix.

S20261109-32.h: Erdoğan visits Azerbaijan for Victory Day, seeks to ease rift with Aliyev
S20261109-32.s: Erdoğan attended Victory Day events in Karabakh and held talks with Aliyev in Shusha. He said those seeking to weaken the alliance cannot succeed, despite recent differences.
S20261109-32.t: Repairs a strained alliance in the South Caucasus.

S20261109-33.h: Democrats may block Trump push to deliver F-35s to Türkiye
S20261109-33.s: Al-Monitor reports Democrats may block a Trump administration effort to deliver F-35 jets to Türkiye and lift sanctions.
S20261109-33.t: Congressional resistance could stall Türkiye's return to the F-35 programme and CAATSA relief.

S20261109-34.h: Erdoğan discusses ending Ukraine war with Trump
S20261109-34.s: Erdoğan discussed efforts to end the war in Ukraine with Trump, hoping intensified diplomacy yields results and pledging continued Türkiye support.
S20261109-34.t: Positions Ankara as a facilitator in Ukraine diplomacy.

S20261109-35.h: Reports of Trump cutting Israel aid shock Israeli defence officials
S20261109-35.s: Israeli defence officials were shocked by a reported Trump cut to aid, with weapons transfers possibly frozen. Trump separately said he dislikes Israel and blamed the war partly for Republican midterm losses.
S20261109-35.t: US-Israel strain would change the regional balance and Washington's approach to Ankara.

S20261109-36.h: Egypt reopens Tripoli embassy, objects to Libya-Türkiye maritime deal
S20261109-36.s: Egypt reopened its embassy in Tripoli after 12 years. In talks with the western government it raised objections to Libya's maritime deal with Türkiye.
S20261109-36.t: Egypt's return challenges Türkiye's position in Libya and the eastern Mediterranean maritime deal.

S20261109-37.h: Iran executes three men over protests and alleged spying for Israel and US
S20261109-37.s: Iran executed three men after the Supreme Court upheld sentences linked to January anti-government protests and alleged spying for Israel and the US. Iranians voiced anger online.

S20261109-38.h: Damascus agrees to women's battalions for YPJ integration
S20261109-38.s: YPJ spokesperson Ruksen Mihemed said Damascus agreed to form two women's battalions of about 400 fighters each. Integration details are still under negotiation. The PYD General Council also met on integration into the Syrian state.
S20261109-38.t: Terms of SDF integration into the Syrian army directly affect Türkiye's security demands.

S20261109-39.h: Iraqi PM threatens force against armed factions; cancels Mosul airport contracts
S20261109-39.s: Iraq's prime minister threatened the full force of law against factions refusing to disarm and cancelled three Mosul airport contracts over alleged militia links. US envoy Tom Barrack praised the move.

S20261109-40.h: Kurdistan delegation in Baghdad negotiates 2027 budget share without deal
S20261109-40.s: A high-level KRG delegation met federal ministers on budget share, customs and oil revenues without agreement yet.

S20261109-41.h: Heavy rain and floods worsen Gaza humanitarian crisis
S20261109-41.s: About 70,000 tents flooded and 350,000 displaced people are without shelter. A sand cliff collapse killed people, and UNICEF warns of a public health crisis. Hamas blames Israel's restrictions on aid and shelter.

S20261109-42.h: US expels Lebanon's consul in Detroit over social media posts
S20261109-42.s: The US State Department ordered the deportation of Lebanon's consul general in Detroit over his posts, saying he has no place in the United States.

S20261109-43.h: Cyprus leaders meet on UN confidence-building measures
S20261109-43.s: Erhürman and Christodoulides meet Monday on two UN-proposed confidence-building measures that will decide whether the talks continue.
S20261109-43.t: The outcome affects Turkish Cypriot diplomacy and Ankara's Cyprus policy.

S20261109-44.h: Yemeni government and Houthi fighting intensifies in Al-Jawf and Marib
S20261109-44.s: Fighting intensified in Marib and Al-Jawf. The Yemeni army says it neutralised 267 Houthi fighters and reports territorial gains, while analysts say Saudi air power has not reversed rebel gains.
